Responsibility to the community — To the address of the Jewish city councillors and public figures

To the address of the Jewish city councillors and public figures.
Every time elections come round for the city council, the Jewish kehilla or some other important body, and the elections do not go favourably for this or that party, people start looking for the guilty, and of course one throws the blame on the other, and in this way they want to discharge their duty towards the voter, to blind him, so that he should not know that he has been sinned against[?] and used not for the good of the community.
Worse still is that every failure is forgotten and no moral is drawn from it for the future, so as to know not to make the same mistakes all over again — mistakes because of which there later arise in the work defects[?], sometimes greater ones.
There is no doubt that the most important body nowadays is the municipal parliament, the city council, which burdens the citizens with local taxes. Not great[?] are the local regulations, to which the citizens must adapt themselves exactly, and both the regulations and the taxes often become questions of life, and it does not always happen that one can adapt to them, if they are adopted without due consideration or clarification. As we know from practice, if a body is not properly represented, the councillors are not properly oriented, and the upshot is that this brings harm to the community.
Thus at the last session of the Będzin city council important economic questions had to be dealt with, which concern in principle the merchant and the small trader. It would seem that in this case our councillors needed to stand on guard and protect the interests of their voters; but "standing on guard" is only a manner of speaking, when they did not turn up in full number, since it is apparently more comfortable at such[?] a time to sit at home. If later there is a failure, Jews will suffer[?]; then one will have to look for an excuse, one will lay it on the other, and somehow they will wriggle out of it.
And in truth, why sacrifice oneself here, when one is sure of the mandate anyway and need not cede it to anyone.
In general, the activity of the Jewish councillors is — let us say it — a dereliction, a paltry, unheard-of one; every councillor is a world unto himself, none takes the other into account, each acts on his own authority, as he wishes and as he pleases. It is clear what value such activity has and what it can look like at all. Besides, the representation, the delegation of Jewish Będzin, is split[?] into small partnerships. A ship without a rudder — and from this, without any doubt, the Jewish community suffers, which can in no way whatsoever be satisfied, even when favours are done for individuals. Our councillors must understand this once and for all, and if they do not understand it, they must be made to understand.
The Jewish voter has the right to demand from his representative intensive, honest public work, and this can happen only when there are[?] common duties binding the community. But as long as this finds no expression, there can be no talk of commitment to the community, which is so badly needed nowadays.
More than once we have heard and written about uniting our councillors into one representation, so that they would be able to represent the whole of Jewish Będzin in a conscious and modern manner, and that we should not have to be disappointed over every trifle and be laughed at before [—], as has happened more than once already.
Is it really no longer possible to find a way out, so that the lawlessness should not reign, which brings shame and mockery on Jewish honour and loses position after position? Can one go on treading this path, on which we make a laughing-stock of ourselves? Can no unity of any kind be created in our ranks, so that we would know beforehand what kind of session we are walking into at the city council and how the questions raised are to be handled?
Surely[?] people would be found who would raise an outcry that an end must be put to the reckless deeds and scandals, that frivolities must no longer be allowed to be committed[?] in the name of the Jewish community, in the name of Jewish society.
That is what must be brought forward at a suitable[?] moment!
* * *
And since we are speaking about the city council, since we are writing about the duties of councillors towards their voters, it is worth mentioning Sosnowiec[?] as well.
We still remember the joy that reigned in the town over the victory of the elected councillors, which came about thanks to Jewish unity.
Who does not remember how fine the beginning was. It was a real delight to watch with what enthusiasm the Jewish representatives came to the sessions and how they were indeed reckoned with. And the truth must be told here, that Jewish Sosnowiec is finely represented in the city council — not only by the number of representatives, but also by the stature of the personalities. Representing[?] in the city council are intelligent people, people with higher education and — most important — people who know how to handle questions and do not allow Jewish honour and pride to be degraded.
That is a great plus nowadays.
When we indeed come as people to sessions with due responsibility and awareness, thanks to which the non-Jewish councillors must, willy-nilly, reckon with them.
But at a time when every time the whole Jewish "Koło" [caucus] was well represented, lately a bit of passivity[?] and frivolity has set in, so much so that they have begun to remain indifferent to the tasks they took upon themselves.
And therefore the Jewish representation must be reminded of this. One must not forget the [importance?] of the moment when one represents the Jewish community, especially in such a time as we are living through.
The Jewish "Koło" must therefore see to it that it continues to be well represented and fulfils its tasks as Jewish Sosnowiec demands of it.
We know that the Jewish "Koło" has achieved much for the town; it is therefore desirable to keep standing on guard and to safeguard everything that is needed. It would also be worthwhile to convene a large meeting for the voters and to give them an account of the work done so far.
Selekt.
An Unheard-of Blackmail (A Letter to the Editor)

[Sosnowiec — letter to the editor.] On the pavement of Sosnowiec, as is known[?], a dark creature has sprung up which has laid its filthy paws on the printed Jewish word and uses it for purposes of blackmail.
The writer of these lines does not intend this time to deal with such an underworld being, because it is simply a disgrace to stand within his four cubits, let alone to polemicize with such a scoundrel, or[?] as he is called here in Sosnowiec...
Unfortunately, however, I am forced to point out publicly what this lawless fellow is capable of.
In the last number of his blackmail rag there appeared a vile pamphlet against the national camp in Sosnowiec. Of course his drivel[?] is, as always, not taken into account this time either; but how astonished[?] I was to see[?] that the pamphlet was signed with my pseudonym, which I have been using since the twenties[?] as a contributor to the "Zaglembier Tsaytung".
For all[?] the readers who, reading the ugly pamphlet, saw my name signed under it, I must state here with bitterness that I have nothing whatsoever to do with it, just as I have nothing at all to do with anything that is scribbled there.
The legal side of this unheard-of blackmail I leave to the above-mentioned editorial office.
Respectfully,
Dr. Papuri.
The Doctor Has Caught the Flu!...

[Humour — feuilleton.] Y. Oberzhanek
You know Doctor Igrek [i.e. "Dr. Y"], of course — a fine little man. A dear little man, soft as satin. Besides[?] being a good man, he is a good doctor. Actually he could have been a good sequestrator [tax bailiff], because he is a good searcher, and when he searches — he finds.
What stones[?] has he not already found in me! I went to him with chilblains[?] — he found in me... kidneys. He searched so long until he found something. I had [—] tonsillitis, in the throat[?] — he found... liver; I had [—] a toe — he detected under the knees... an appendix ["blind gut"]. He holds by "I laboured and I found" — whoever searches, finds; so he searches until he finds.
And he, the eternal searcher, my family doctor — whenever anything happens, one sends for him, and since he is a dear man, a refined man, soft as satin, he comes at every call. He is already so much one of the family that he comes just like that, to take a look how things are, and on the occasion he at least[?] gives a little feel, a search — perhaps he will find something. I am already so well acquainted with him that I know in advance what he will say. He comes into the house, I stretch out on the sofa[?], and before you know it I turn over with my "not-before-your-honour"[?] upward, and as soon as he takes out the "słuchawka" [stethoscope], I immediately start "breathing" [dychać]; I know when one has to "breathe deeply" and when one has to stop "breathing" altogether.
I am already so well acquainted with him that I don't wait until he tells me to do something — I do everything myself; even his prescriptions are already familiar to me. I know in advance what he will give me.
This week my wife felt a bit poorly[?]: she had a bit of stabbing, a bit of aching, a bit of coughing and a bit of sneezing, so I went straight to my family doctor.
"Proszę", whom do you want? — the maid asks me at the door.
"What do you mean, whom? I don't need you — I need the doctor."
"Doktor nie przyjmuje" [the doctor is not receiving] — she [—] informed[?] me.
"Co w gości?"[?] — I asked.
"Pan doktor leży" [the doctor is lying down] — she explained to me.
"Śpi?" [Is he asleep?]
"Nie śpi, leży w łóżku" [not asleep, he is lying in bed].
"Leży? To niech wstanie!" [Lying? Then let him get up!] — I answered her.
"Przepraszam bardzo, doktor leży na grypę" [very sorry, the doctor is down with the flu].
"Na grypę? Doktor na grypę?" — I did not understand what she was babbling. Can a doctor also be ill with the flu? And perhaps he really is ill — then one must visit the sick, especially a man who is like family. Where is it written that I must always be ill and he healthy — why shouldn't it be the other way round for once? Why should he always come to me and give me advice, and why shouldn't I for once come to him and give him advice? So I went in to him, into the bedroom, to visit the sick.
I come in, take a look at him, and I am seized with great pity for him: his neck bandaged with cotton wool, his head tied up with a cloth[?], lying in a nightshirt, with a [—], white as the wall[?] — exactly the way I look when he comes to me.
"Good morning, Herr Doctor!" — I said in the same tone in which he comes to me — "What's the matter with you? Aren't you ashamed? A doctor lying down with the flu too?"
"Yes, yes, a doctor is a human being too" — he answered.
"Yes, that I know now; until now I did not know it. Panie doktorze, perhaps we should call a doctor?"
"Eh, no need, it will pass!"
The whole business already annoyed me: why doesn't he say so when he comes to me? Why, when I am ill, does he say one needs a doctor, and he doesn't? If he has no faith in doctors, why should I have faith in them?
And all of a sudden it occurred to me: maybe he is right? Maybe he really needs no doctors[?]? After all I know what he does to me — I will do the same to him. I say to him:
"Panie doktorze, turn over with your doctorly 'z przeproszeniem' [if you'll excuse the expression] upward."
He looks at me with a pair of goggling eyes:
"What for?"
"What do you mean, what for? Why don't I ask you when you tell me to turn over? Turn over, Panie doktorze, and I'll 'zbadać' [examine] you, I'll listen to you; first you'll breathe 'głęboko' [deeply] and then you won't breathe at all."
"Eh, no need" — he answered.
"What do you mean, no need? How do you know there's no need? Lie down, perhaps I'll find something in you."
"Panie doktorze, open your mouth."
"What for?"
"Perhaps it's 'żołądkowe' [something gastric]."
"What's got into you?"[?]
"Panie doktorze, just show me your pulse."
"A doctor has no pulse."
"Never mind, I'll find it."
"Panie doktorze, where is your 'słuchawka'?"
"What do you need it for?"
"I'll put it to your lungs, to your heart, I'll hear how it beats."
"You know a fever[?] [i.e. nothing]. A doctor has no heart at all."
"Perhaps I should put cupping glasses on you?"
"Eh, that you'd actually do well — can you put on cupping glasses?"
"What a question! If you are my family doctor, shouldn't I be able to put on cupping glasses?" The maid held a candle, the doctor turned over his gracious[?] "how-do-you-call-it", and I put on the cupping glasses; the doctor had great pleasure. Where is it written that he must always stand at my bed while I groan[?] — let it be the other way round for once...
After the cupping glasses I sat down at his writing desk and started writing. He asks me:
"What are you writing?"
"You'll hear in a moment. You will take three times daily eight[?] [—] drops, on an empty stomach ten fainting drops, on the throat a compress of room-temperature water with spirit, you will gargle your throat with Chinosol, and before sleep — aspirin."
He burst out laughing:
"How do you know that?"
"What do you mean, how do I know? If you are my family doctor, shouldn't I know?"
Before leaving I started palpating his belly. He asks:
"What are you feeling for?"
"Do I know? Perhaps I'll find something in you — perhaps a little water, perhaps a little lime, perhaps kidneys, gall, or a little liver? Listen to me, Panie doktorze, let me search — you'll see, I'll find something!.."
Now I am just coming from my doctor. I had real satisfaction. Only one thing annoys me: that I didn't charge him for the visit.
That, gentlemen, is how a doctor looks when he himself is lying down with the flu...
Jews of Sosnowiec, How Long?

(More on the campaign for the Jewish hospital.)
Lately we have had occasion to read in the press brief reports from the committee formed to restore the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec to health. From these brief reports one can see that the committee reproaches[?] the collectors, saying that their initiative is a political one.
With this argument the committee explains the hitherto[?] unsuccessful campaign to collect the necessary sum.
And the question arises: what is the reason for the whole campaign? In my opinion the reason is a deeper one. For what good child needs its parents to preach morals to it, and what bad pupil is helped by the supervision of many teachers?
The good child always walks „the straight path“, whereas the bad pupil is not helped even by the greatest supervision. Parents and educators can confirm this too.
In medicine, too, it is accepted that a „good illness“ heals very well with weaker help, while a bad one needs stronger help.
These are the secrets of human nature, which is a part of the nature of the world. More than one of its creators[?] has fallen as a victim before its gates, but the secrets of today's human character are easier to explain.
The character of today's man, with all due respect, has grown somewhat weaker with regard to human suffering. Today's man is not as carried away[?] by social need as in the past; he does not react so quickly to every event, as long as he does not see the terrible picture of life before his own eyes.
What does he care that his poor brother needs a hospital, where he must be operated on immediately, and at home there is not a grosz in cash, no food, no care? What does it interest him that his poor sister must be admitted to a maternity institution, to a proper clinic? That the poor child must be operated on, that the belatedly treated diphtheria is choking him in the throat, that an accident has happened, the child has broken a leg and must be treated in a hospital?
A characteristic fact: at the beginning of the World War the writer of these lines knew a Jewish director of a factory, a very rich man, who boasted to me that he lived in 20 luxury rooms and was not afraid of typhus. It turned out, however, that even such a luxury apartment could not protect against the terrible disease. A few months later the director, unfortunately, died of that very disease.
In medicine it is known: whoever wants to be healthy must have healthy neighbours; whoever wants to be clean must have clean neighbours. That is, everyone must also take care that his neighbour be healthy, have something to eat, keep himself hygienic — then one is safer. On the contrary, in time of an epidemic the microbe is a democrat: it crawls boldly into the comfortable salons just as into the attics and cellar dwellings.
These are the main arguments that compel every thinking Jew to care for the health of his brethren, because these are the most elementary duties of mankind, of which the Jews were the first architects!
Let them not, God forbid, be the last today!
Is it not then a crying injustice that we should have to awaken the conscience of our rich men to give money for the hospital just now, when we are already almost tired of awakening it?
Or is the collector to blame when he is shown the door, or at best given pennies there where he counts on being received with open arms?
A short time ago I read in the „Zaglembier Tsaytung“ a short notice reporting that well-known Jewish industrialists had given 12 thousand zł. for the winter relief. The news greatly pleased me, seeing that the Jewish heart burns with compassion at all times, for all; and I have, God forbid, nothing against it. But how great my joy would have been if at least 5 such donors could be found for our hospital — then there would be an end to all the committees, to the whole tararam [hullabaloo], for it is already the highest [time] to free the hospital's managers from other worries; their worry must be only for the good of the patients.
— Jews, merciful sons of the merciful, fulfil your duty, then, and do not make a mockery and a disgrace of our priceless treasure[?] — the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec.
Herman Szer, Będzin.
The Richest Family in the World.

Whoever thinks that Vanderbilt or Rockefeller are the richest people in the world is greatly mistaken. True, they too lack nothing of this world's goods, but the truly richest person in the world lives in Japan.
Anyone who does business with Japan and obtains goods from there — no matter whether they are big machines or cheap toothbrushes — sees on the crates that arrive from there a small four-cornered field with three strokes inside it. In Japanese this is called "Mitsui", or in our language "three wells".
This mark is the emblem of the richest family not only in Japan, but indeed in the whole world.
A few years ago I met at the Leipzig fair the head of the Mitsui family, Baron Tam[?] Mitsui, who told me interesting details about this family.
Some three hundred years ago their great-great-grandfather found in three wells on his small plot of land a great treasure, which thieves had probably hidden there, and this very treasure brought him great luck in his trade. He took the name "Mitsui" (three wells), and since then the word has meant: great trade all over the world.
The business, which always passes from generation to generation, has grown ever bigger and bigger, and today it covers three quarters of all the trade in Japan itself and almost the whole of Japan's exports to the world.
The Mitsui family has its own laws, which are very strict towards its own family members, by virtue of a special privilege from the government. All Mitsuis must submit to these family laws. Today there are eleven "Mitsui" families in Japan; the eldest of each family sits on a supreme council, which "rules and reigns" not only over the fortune but also over the persons of the Mitsui family. From among the eleven families a president is elected (not always the eldest of the family), who has the decisive word in the family.
All family members must be employed in their businesses; if it turns out[?] that one has no interest in trade, the supreme council can expel him from the family — he must change his name and has nothing more to do with the Mitsuis[?]. The supreme council can also admit into the family a total stranger who is capable in trade, and allow him to bear the name "Mitsui". Every young man who finishes school in Japan must continue his studies at a university in England.
The Mitsuis today own more merchant ships than France and England together; with their ships they send goods to the four corners of the earth.
They have giant[?] factories in Japan that produce everything people need, from cannons to trouser buttons.
They live very simply, in plain wooden houses; many members of the family are mostly not at home at all. They are busy in their various factories, or they travel abroad on various big business affairs.
They have founded towns of their own, where the various kinds of manufacture are carried out. Thus, for example, the place where they manufacture steel goods is called "Saligen" [i.e. Solingen]. Beer they make in a place to which they gave the name Pilsen. Since the names of towns are not protected anywhere, they can sell "genuine Solingen steel" and "genuine[?] Pilsner beer" and so on and so forth...
They are the biggest taxpayers in Japan, and when I asked Baron Mitsui how much he estimates the fortune of the Mitsuis, he answered me:
"Exact figures I cannot give; this much is certain — that our fortune is greater than the fortunes of all the world's rich men together."
Z. Haber, Vienna.
Clarification from the Keren Hayesod Committee in Sosnowiec.

The breaking-up of this year's Keren Hayesod "academy" (gala evening) in Sosnowiec greatly agitated, as is generally known, Jewish society in Zagłębie. In spite of this the Sosnowiec Keren Hayesod committee did not react to this base act, because it was hard to admit the thought that any persons[?] could really have anything in common with an organisation that supposedly strives for "the Kingdom of Israel". But as soon as this organisation publicly declared (in the "Zaglembier Tsaytung", No. 7) that the "khlaptses" [Polish chłopcy, "lads"] who ran wild at the Keren Hayesod academy are its own — as they put it in their statement, "90 per cent of the audience were Revisionists" — we hold that "a litigant's admission is worth a hundred witnesses", and one can no longer pass over[?] it in silence.
And in connection with their statement we find it necessary to clarify the following:
1) It is indeed true that the Revisionists did not force their way into the municipal theatre, but bought tickets at the box office; this circumstance, however, does not change the shameful fact that for more than an hour these same people did not let Dr. Melarista[?], Rabbi Hager or Mr. Gerbowski get a word in.
2) We confirm categorically that the report in "Haynt" about the shameful shouts of the Revisionists corresponds to reality. During their rampage the Revisionists did not stop shouting: "Down with the Vira-katuga[?]!", "We will not allow money to be taken out of Poland", and other such cries. We also find it necessary to remind the academy-wreckers that besides the "fine" shouts reported in "Haynt", they also did not spare insults addressed to many members of the academy's presidium.
3) Without going into the reasons for which a certain young man committed suicide — since there is evidence that he did it on grounds that have nothing in common with any striving for aliyah to Eretz Israel — the academy presidium is not aware that the wreckers proposed to honour his memory by standing, simply because the bacchanalia in the hall was so great that nothing could be heard.
4) If such a proposal was indeed brought in by the wreckers amid the great uproar, it testifies all the more to their baseness, because only the presidium is entitled to propose honouring anyone's memory, not every ticket-buyer.
5) The academy was dissolved by the presidium, but upon[?] the urgent demand of representatives[?] of the authorities. The Keren Hayesod committee in Sosnowiec is very pleased that by the timely closing of the academy a bloody brawl was avoided — one about which part of the Polish press afterwards reported falsely, and at which the academy-wreckers had aimed with their rampage.
6) Expressing the sharpest protest against the Revisionist organisation for bringing into the Zionist street such methods of struggle, which are alien not only to the Zionist and Jewish spirit but are also against the most elementary rules of decency, the Keren Hayesod committee in Sosnowiec welcomes with great satisfaction the pleasing fact that the Sosnowiec Keren Hayesod contributors have already given their worthy answer to the academy-wreckers and their "awakener" leaders[?] through their mass voluntary contributions to the building of Eretz Israel.
The Keren Hayesod Committee in Sosnowiec.
When It's Not Meant to Be...

P. Blumenkranz (Częstochowa [?])
(A sketch).

Twice already Miss Zelikowicz had "been viewed" (at a match-making meeting). True, years ago she thought nothing of it; God forbid — as she put it — a match arranged by a matchmaker was legalized prostitution. She had read so many books and knew how wonderful it is when two young people meet and their hearts come to an understanding...

But it was a lost cause: life — as she later justified herself — is stronger than all theories, especially when her parents would by no means leave her in peace. Her father only grumbled and did not talk to her at all, while her mother never stopped tormenting her:
— Nachesh, what will the end be after all [?] — you're getting not younger but older; luck keeps you waiting, the big win!

She got angry at her mother and shouted. But with time she began quietly to agree with her. All that "patience" — time, [—], nerves — is not worth any "[—]"; when he has bought you [?] a cinema ticket, heaven already opens; "having fun" (bawić się) — why not; but no more than that. No, men are terrible egoists, and only money: a girl may be as "pretty" [?] as you like — if you don't pay up, nothing even begins.

Up to now she had been "viewed" twice. The first time with a sympathetic merchant even, but he argued that without money he could not marry.

Her father had already wanted to "do" something: borrow a few thousand zł. for a couple of weeks and deposit them at the P.K.O. [Postal Savings Bank], "to throw dust in his eyes" [?]; but the young man, it seems, was no fool, and demanded precisely that the money be paid into a bank in [—] [?]. That is how things are done — the matchmaker argued on his behalf — all over the world, and his voice trembled: a lot [?] can still come of this match.

The young lady was at that time very indignant with her parents:
— What do you want of me? Let there be no love, but luck I must have, like Bale. Wamperstein [?], a manager with gold teeth, fell in love with her "at first sight" (Polish: z pierwszego spojrzenia).

The second "viewing" took place in another town, at a cousin's. The suitor was no longer in his first youth, but that was not the flaw. Often it is better to have a "steady salary" (stała pensja) [?]; but God alone in heaven knows — as soon as she cast her first glance at him she nearly felt ill. Nothing [?] about him was sympathetic! He was short and plump as a barrel, with a long hooked nose and red hands like a washerwoman's [?]; he had sparse, glossy hair with a parting [?] in the middle and lacquered nails with red varnish. He talked only about leather and [—] (he was a partner in a tannery), and was looking only for a "thrifty, housewifely" (gospodarna) girl. Money isn't everything — he told her openly — money gives no security. He likes a wife to be "[—]", lunch to be on time, etc. He has an acquaintance with a beautiful wife but an outlandish [—], with whom he would not have lived even two weeks. "Imagine, for breakfast [?] she runs to the shop to buy her husband a [roll?]! And what kind of order there is in her linen cupboard — don't even ask! A woman must [—] in the household!" And as he said this he smiled and showed his strange, large gold teeth on both sides.

— Mama, — Nache later burst out crying — I'll become an old maid, I'll wait until I have grey braids, but him [—] I won't marry; I have a terrible "disgust" (wstręt) for him, he is so repulsive! She cried bitterly and her mother stroked her hair:
— Never mind. There is no Jewish convent. The Almighty does not abandon even a worm in the earth — surely He won't abandon you. Well, enough crying already...

Today they were expecting the third candidate. First thing in the morning Nachshe (Nache) ran to the hairdresser; she did not want to end up with a "kalpika" [?]. Today she would also have a "[—]" done — it's modern and makes one look very [?] young.

The mother's cheeks were flushed as if she had coloured them with red paper, and she had been bustling about since early morning. She borrowed a "[—]" [?] from the neighbour and began first thing in the morning to prepare the reception. She wanted to buy Spanish oranges — they are smaller and [—] [?] — but [—] [?] wouldn't allow it!
— Mama, sometimes it must be [?] a groschen for a rogal (crescent roll) and sometimes a rogal for a groschen. — Then they discussed every little detail: what kind of "mieszanka" (assorted sweets) to buy, which biscuits for the tea, etc.

The father had no mind for all these trifles; he had experience of the earlier "viewings", and shrugging his shoulders he grumbled:
— You're just a simple woman. If the world were as it used to be — he explained in a Talmud-study chant — I would count out five thousand roubles and would practically have the say! But for our many sins, today, what can I know? Either he'll be worth nothing, or he'll demand cash — you understand?
— Well, [—] [?] father, show what you can do! What do you think — that Nachele is 18 today? Let's see indeed what you can accomplish, by all means!
— I really think that if "[—]" [?], I'd know what to do [?].
— And your brother can't help you out at all? Such a [—] year [?] on him — what kind of brother is he.

They began to quarrel in earnest, throwing at each other all their sins since the wedding; but meanwhile the daughter came home and the house filled up with her. The hairdo really suited her, she looked younger. The mother set aside her "heartache" [?] and helped her daughter dress; they immediately laid out the chocolates, carefully, like etrogs, and set them in the cupboard. In the end they did buy Jaffa oranges, and also took out of the cupboard a small bottle of wine, already 6—7 years old. The old man combed his beard and they began to wait. The mother stationed herself [?] at the window; every rustle at the door startled everyone in the house.

Nache pretended to make nothing of it all and hummed [?] a popular tune, but her heart pounded like a robber's. She was already sick of being inspected and wanted to jump out of her skin, because all day long they sigh over her head and treat her as if she were dead.

But as she stood thus at the window, everything suddenly went dark before the mother's eyes: Mendel the matchmaker, in an unbuttoned [coat?] [—], is already running; he sends his goatee ahead of him and his coat-tails tangle between his big boots.
— Reb Shloyme, you hear, [—], good morning to you, I'm "flustered" [?], but it's nothing — a little mishap has happened; but one mustn't despair entirely: everything is in the hands of Heaven except colds and chills. You hear, Reb Shloyme, this very moment I received a postcard — here [?], read: flu, God preserve us. But never mind, all beginnings are hard; he must lie in bed, as you know, [—] [?] of eighteen days, and afterwards he'll write separately. Yes, and to tell the truth, not wanting to fool myself, I don't like [—] [?] — what does "write separately" mean: Elijah with a thorn in tow? But he is a splendid vessel, I tell you; from what I've been told, never in his life has he transgressed a "[—]" [?]; [—] [?], a merchant can't be so [—] [?]. [—] [?]. Well-established merchants, solid firms — yes.

He fell silent in the middle and sighed, a deep sigh, which — according to the Talmud — breaks half a person's body. He had thought he would be able to straighten his bones — and here you go, a fresh affliction: flu. The oranges, layered with "[—]" [?] in fruit bowls, stood on the cupboard as if ashamed.

Reb Shloyme took his combed beard in his hand, crumpled it as over a difficult Talmudic passage, and [put it] between his teeth.
— I felt it wouldn't go smoothly; my intuition doesn't fool me — he did not forget to boast, even at such a moment.
— Enough, he's talked himself out — his wife wouldn't let him finish, and [turned?] [?], ashamed and trembling, to the daughter:
— Nachele, go out for a little walk, it's a beautiful day, a sin to sit at home.
— — — — — —
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Tetzaveh)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Tetzaveh
—o—
a) "Pure olive oil, beaten, for the light" (printed "27:3" [?]; = Ex. 27:20)
"...pure and beaten for the light, but not pure and beaten for the meal-offerings. Might one think that pure beaten oil is unfit for meal-offerings? Scripture says (Exodus 29) 'and a tenth of fine flour mingled with beaten oil.' If so, why does it say 'for the light'? Because the Torah has pity on the money of Israel." Menachot 86.
The question arises: why with meal-offerings did the Torah have pity on the money of Israel, but not with the Menorah? Why must there be no "pure beaten" oil for meal-offerings, for the sake of saving, because "the Torah has pity on the money of Israel," while with the Menorah no attention is paid to this and it must specifically be "pure beaten"?
Because the meal-offerings symbolise money, livelihood, and there one must be restrained, thrifty [?]; whereas the Menorah symbolises knowledge, wisdom, and there "the Torah has pity on the money of Israel" no longer applies — there is no saving when it comes to Torah and knowledge... Yalkut Yehuda.
—o—
b) "And you shall speak to all the wise-hearted" (Ex. 28:3)
Since Moses here took costly garments for his brother Aaron, a suspicion could have arisen that he was after his brother's wealth; therefore God told him to choose wise-hearted people, clever people — because it is always only fools who are full of suspicion... Imrei Chen.
—o—
c) "Stones of remembrance for the children of Israel" (ibid., printed "11"; the verse is 28:12)
"That the Holy One, blessed be He, should see the tribes written before Him and remember their righteousness." Rashi.
The merit of the forefathers must first of all be "stones of remembrance for the children of Israel" — it is not God who must remember the merit of the forefathers, but first of all the Jews. If Jews do not remember their forefathers and do not walk in their ways, then it is even worse for them when God recalls their good forefathers. Only when the merit of the forefathers will be "stones of remembrance for the children of Israel," when Jews will remember what kind of forefathers they had — only then "and Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord": Aaron will be able to remind God of the Jews' merit of the forefathers.. Ktav Sofer.
—o—
d) "And you shall make a breastplate of judgment" (ibid., 15)
"The breastplate atones for judgment, as it is written: the breastplate of judgment." Arakhin 16.
What does "atones for judgment" mean? Is judgment then a sin? Yes — many a time one sins by holding to strict judgment where one should apply mercy. Therefore Aaron atoned for the sin of judgment, because Aaron was a lover of peace and a pursuer of peace, and that is how one must be even in judgment: with the attribute of strict justice alone the world could not have existed, and the attribute of mercy had to be mixed in... Leket Amarim.
• • •
And that is why the names of the tribes were engraved on the breastplate — to show that before the law all Jews are equal: there are no important and unimportant tribes; all are engraved in their chronological order, "you shall not respect persons in judgment" — all are equal before the law. R' Yehuda Leib Ginzburg.
—o—
e) "A golden bell and a pomegranate" (ibid., 34)
"Even the sinners of Israel among you are full of commandments like a pomegranate" [doubtful reading]. Midrash.
That is what the pomegranate, which is part of the bell, means: the commandments of the sinners of Israel, too, are like a pomegranate, like a bell. When a sinner of Israel once does a good deed, he rings it out to the whole world... Migdal David.
—o—
f) "And its sound shall be heard when he goes into the holy place before the Lord" (ibid., 35)
R' Chaim Brisker [of Brisk, Brześć] used to say about the Hasidim who shout while praying:
On the High Priest one had to hang little bells, so that one could hear how he comes in to pray in the Holy of Holies and how he goes out from there; had the High Priest been accustomed [to behave] like a Hasidic rebbe, there would have been no need to hang little bells on him — he would have raised such a noise that one would have heard him from far away...
—o—
g) "And you shall make an altar to burn incense" ([—]:1; Ex. 30:1)
The commentators ask: why does the section of the incense altar not stand above, among the Temple vessels, but at the end of the portion? How does it come here?
Because incense atones for slander (Yoma 44); therefore it is placed next to the section of the shekels, because shekels [money] are [?] a cause of slander and gossip.. R' Yitzchak Moshe of Kelm.
—o—
h) "The one lamb you shall offer in the morning" (Ex. 29:39)
In biblical times there were idolaters who served the sun, and others who served the moon. Baal was the idol of the sun, and Asherah — the goddess of the moon. The sun-worshippers practised [?] their idolatry at sunrise towards the east side, and the moon-worshippers — towards the west side, at the rising of the moon.
Therefore we were commanded to offer sacrifices to God in the morning and in the evening, to show that for us neither the sun nor the moon are gods; and that is why the Gemara says (beginning of chapter 4 of Tamid): "The morning daily offering was slaughtered in the west, and the evening daily offering was slaughtered in the east" — the reverse of the idolaters. R' Hillel HaBavli.
• • •
Hence it is understandable why, at the close of the Sabbath, in the hymn "Eliyahu HaNavi" we say: "a man who raged against the sun-worshippers" — a man who was angry at the sun-worshippers. The question arises: when did Elijah quarrel with sun-worshippers? Where is this mentioned in the Bible?
But according to what was said, that Baal was the sun-god, it is understandable: that Elijah fought against the worshippers of Baal is, after all, told in the Bible. Kirya Ne'emana.
On the Renewal of „Tarbut“

[Będzin — Hebrew culture and education; „Tarbut“.]
Neta Landner.
In the din of everyday life, in which every individual has to wage a stubborn struggle for his existence, in the hard and bitter struggle that the Jewish community has to wage nowadays, the most important attribute of our national existence — Hebrew culture — has been pushed aside almost entirely; the concentration of all our attention and alertness [?] on our economic positions has put our spiritual-cultural problems in the shade. The Jewish people, the „People of the Book“, forgets — because of its troubles — the rule „man does not live by bread alone“; gone are the times of old, when, in a time of trouble, God forbid, every individual found his consolation in the „Book of Books“, in the life of the spirit; the community as well as the individual found rest for its pained [?] and suffering soul. Our poet Bialik, of blessed memory, felt the nation's grief most deeply and immortalized it [?] in his well-known poem „Im yesh et nafshekha lada'at“ („If you would know“), in which the secret of our existence is revealed, despite the long, thorny path of martyrdom. The Jewish press, which ought in fact to be the tone-setter of Jewish public life, is also swept along by the current of shallowness, by day-to-day events, and seldom have you found an echo in the press (with the exception of the Hebrew „Baderekh“) of our spiritual and cultural problems (not counting the recently arisen discussion around Sholem Asch about Hebrew and Yiddish). Even our higher Zionist bodies, in view of the constant defensive struggle that has to be waged on the Eretz Israel front, have neglected Hebrew cultural work, which forms an integral part of our renaissance movement; all the solemn Congress resolutions about „Tarbut“ have not been carried out. The Zionist [printed „Bionist“] activists, being always absorbed by various fund-raising campaigns for the upbuilding of Eretz Israel, never find time to reflect on the very essence of Zionism. It is an unforgivable crime on the part of all the Zionist activists, who devote their time to all kinds of public work, even such as is in contradiction with pure Zionist principles, while for „Tarbut“ work they lack time and initiative. This is not the place to depict the whole complex of the „Tarbut“ question. That would lead me too far; it is enough to point to the sad phenomenon that in such a mother-city in Israel as our town is, no evil eye, the initiators who would want to devote themselves to founding a „Tarbut“ folk school have not yet been found. It is simply a disgrace that in such a [unclear word] Jewish town as Zawiercie there does exist a Tarbut school and [kindergartens? — unclear word], while [our town], which distinguishes itself in all campaigns, lacks the Zionist ambition to found a Hebrew folk school. When we look at the rapid process of assimilation that takes place in the state elementary schools [Polish powszechne] on the one hand, and at the terrible ignorance that reigns even among the so-called national-Zionist youth on the other, the great cry must burst forth which our poet Bialik, of blessed memory, hurled at Polish Jewry 5 years ago, during his stay in Poland: „Back to the heder!“ And if Bialik managed to strike fear into Polish Jewry in view of the emptiness and ignorance of the Jewish street, we today, when ignorance has already seized almost the whole of Jewish youth, must surely, surely storm, find no rest and oppose the current of shallowness by every means.
It is therefore to be welcomed that a small group of young people have taken the initiative to revive „Tarbut“ activity in Będzin. The beginning was made with the opening of the library and the arranging of Hebrew talks every week. May your hands be strengthened.
It is now the duty of the Zionist activists to come to the aid of the small group, to help develop „Tarbut“, and perhaps this will finally bring about the realization of the ideal of creating a Tarbut folk school. If only!
—o—
[Notice — League for Labour Palestine; Tel Hai.]
Communiqué of the League for Labour Eretz Israel
The Central Committee of the League for Labour Eretz Israel in Poland has issued an appeal for the campaign of 11 Adar, which falls on the 17th anniversary of the death of Trumpeldor and his comrades, the heroes of Tel Hai.
On 11 Adar, 22 February, academies and evenings dedicated to the memory of the heroes of Tel Hai will take place throughout the country.
A great collection campaign will also be held for the fund of the Eretz Israel workers — for the KPAI [Kupat Poalei Eretz Israel] (Palestine Workers' Fund).
At the same time the campaign will be conducted among individuals and institutions.
Because the campaign for the KKL [Jewish National Fund] is held during Purim week, the campaign for the P.A.F. [Palestine Workers' Fund] will begin on 7 March, when the Youth Day for Labour Eretz Israel takes place.
Thousands of young people will then visit Jewish homes and workplaces for the mass campaign of the PAF.
Only 38...

[Humour — the “Der Kokh-lefl” (The Cooking Ladle) page; dialogue; followed by “Asked and Answered”.] Der Kokh-lefl. Humour and satire. Compiled by Amotsli.
(A dialogue between a patient and an “Ubezpieczalnia” [social-insurance fund] doctor)
The doctor to the Jewish patient: What do you want?
Patient: With respect, would the Herr Doctor please come on a house call to my girl; she has been ill for 2 days already.
Doctor: Does she have a fever?
Patient: Of course she does — I haven’t measured how much she has!
Doctor: Listen, I will come, but if she turns out not to have 38, you will have to pay for the visit.
Patient: My dear sir [“panie, lebn”], [—?] and if she has 37 and a few tenths, is that too little?
Doctor: No — only a full 38...
Patient: Let it be 38 then — do I have a choice? All right, let it be as the Herr Doctor wishes...
—o—
Asked and Answered.
1.
— What is the difference between a deceased person and a merchant?
— The deceased one forgets, and the merchant one never forgets... (with exceptions).
2.
— What is the difference between a cantor and a communal activist?
— Both of them stand with their back to the people...
3.
— What is the difference between the “urząd” [the government office / tax office] and the moon?
— At the “urząd” they shake out your pockets every day, and at the moon once a month (the Blessing of the New Moon).
Lejb Sztabiński.
What “irks” him.

[Humour — “Der Kokh-lefl”; joke.] Two brothers: one is a great pauper and the other a rich man. The other day the poor brother fell ill. Seeing that things were grave, the rich brother came to pay him a sick-call. Says the sick man:
— You see, Mendl, I am soon going there, where there is no poor and rich, where everyone is equal.
— Yosl, spare me your communist propaganda — the rich brother replied angrily.
Catarrhism. (On the influenza epidemic).

[Humour — “Der Kokh-lefl”; mock-medical feuilleton.] What actually is a catarrh?
As is known, influenza begins with a catarrh; in this connection we set out the meaning of catarrh and how to guard against the catarrh epidemic, which has a habit of crawling into everyone’s nose.
The catarrh is a kind of sniffle-dictator, which leads everyone by the nose... His seat is his favourite spot, “the tower”, located between a person’s eyes; it is in just such a “tower” that the dictator Mussolini sits in Rome.. (he too is afraid of a hot compress...)
To this day the bacillus that causes catarrh has not been established. Feldshers [medical orderlies] establish that their[?] bacillus is called “Pay up!” [“batsol” — a pun on “batsil”, bacillus]... Dr. Pesing[?] maintains that catarrh can be removed by “hypnosis”[?].
So far it has not been possible to determine whether catarrh is proletarian or aristocratic [“pritsish” — of the squire class]. There are two schools of thought:
Some claim that catarrh is truly proletarian, for when it enters the nose there is an upheaval there, the stomach goes on strike, and the tip of the nose turns red.
Others, on the contrary, say that catarrh is of aristocratic descent, and the proof: it likes to enter the nose, where there are two “entrances”, and as soon as it gets into the stomach it keeps on [—] [?] food-worry[?].
The sum total of a catarrh.
Catarrh belongs to the contagious diseases; thus, for example, someone may have a dollar along with a catarrh, and when he holds out his hand to another, he will pass him only the catarrh itself.
For young people and for the married, catarrh with its sneezing is a misfortune: it happens that a girl declares her love to someone and he sneezes — and it seems to her that he is confirming it...
M A T A.
The faithful husband. A conversation at the sick fund.

[Humour — “Der Kokh-lefl”; sketch.] In the waiting room [“poczekalnia”] of the sick fund several women and one man sit and chat.
First woman: — I tell you, this whole business of getting married doesn’t pay. I am already three years past the wedding, and all that time my husband hasn’t yet spent a single evening at home.
The second: — Yes, yes, all men are scoundrels [“podlece”].
— Now, now — said the man — I, for example, was married for ten years, and in all that time I didn’t budge from the house.
— Ah, that was true love.
— No, that was paralysis.
Antiques collected for the Zagłębie museum.

[Humour — “Der Kokh-lefl”; Będzin — local satire.] Since there are plans to open a museum in the Będzin castle, and the Zagłębie public is surely curious to know what will be found there, we give here a list of the antiques that will be there:
The interpellation that the Jewish town councillors submitted to the town council.
A genuine (not a counterfeit) złoty, which a Sosnowiec “philanthropist” gave to an institution.
A paid-up promissory note.
A pair of whole trousers belonging to a local merchant.
A motor car that has not yet run anyone over.
One will also be able to see portraits:
Of a Zagłębie merchant who has not yet been under “nadzór” [court supervision of an insolvent business].
Of a landlord who has not yet thrown any tenant out of the flat.
A communal activist who has not yet been caught[?] in the act..
A modern little wife who has never had a “zastępca”[?] [a “deputy”, i.e. a lover].
We have it good. Topical rhymes.

[Humour — “Der Kokh-lefl”; satirical poem — emigration and territorialism.] That Jews have it bitter —
how dare one say so,
it’s a sin[?], upon my life,
to complain now.
Who says that we are hated
in the lands,
that they won’t let us
anywhere near the lectern —
the story is a lie,
it’s [?] an antique,
there’s actually beginning[?]
good fortune for the Jews...
People chase after us
with tremendous force,
they fight over us
as over gold, as over oil.
Here comes one Blum [Léon Blum, French premier]
from free Paris
and gives us, upon my life,
a sizeable[?] surprise —
for our sake he has
simply gone down on his knees,
he is already presenting us
with the whole world...
New Caledonia —
becomes a Jewish street,
“Nobiga”[?], [?] —
quite seriously, no joke,
and if that’s too little,
there’s no danger either,
they throw in as a bonus
Madagascar...
And if there are still too few
salvations without end,
they give us America
as an outright gift..
And still more territories
of the best kind,
[—?] the stove[?]
and safely sheltered.
You lie there on the beach [“plaża”]
the whole year round,
you may let your hair
grow down to your belt...
You may go without underpants,
none of that is needed —
a land on the equator[?]
is real schmaltz...
With red Indians —
it’s a real stroke of luck...
In short, my friends —
we have it fine and good.
Shmelke.
"Khaptomania" [Grab-mania]

[Humour — feuilleton.] (Feuilleton.) By A. M. Kayzer.
"Khaptomania" means, in plain Yiddish, "khapenish" (grabbing). It is a typical trait that plays an important role in our everyday life.
True, grabbing is something of a matter among other peoples too, for what are the poor things to do when, for our many sins, this is a world of nothing but grab-and-gulp. Everyone grabs and everything gets grabbed — so they grab too. But there is a big difference between our grabbing and theirs — a grab, from our "grab-kheshnos"[?] to theirs; after all, they are gentile heads, so their grabbing is done in a gentile manner too.
Italy, for example, grabbed a piece of Abyssinia; in Germany they grab socialists and lock[?] them up; in Russia they grab Zionists and exile[?] them; in Eretz Israel they catch illegal[?] tourists and deport them; in America gangsters grab respectable people in order to grab ransom money afterwards.
Our grabbing, however, has quite a different face. With us, one will[?] not grab countries or people — pfui, that is "kholshi-khalashes"[?]! Paskudstvo [an abomination]! It's not at all befitting our dignity! In general it is not at all practical, because countries and people have to be kept — you have to give them food — and where are we to take it from, when we ourselves "lay our teeth on the shelf" [are starving]? So with us one grabs such everyday things as require no food; we grab such spiritual eternities that come with "shehi pehi"[?]; at such kinds of grabbing we are great creatures, real experts; grabbing is a constant process with us. We are the "permanent ones"[?] among eternal grabbers — our whole life is one grabbed thing.
As soon as a Jew "grabs himself up" (jumps out of bed) in the morning, he "grabs himself" straight out into the street to grab a little earning[?]; if he catches it — good; if not, he grabs a loan, grabs an interest-free loan, as long as his "so-and-so" (wife) doesn't grab him by the coat-tail...
A Jew doesn't go to someone — he "grabs himself over"...
A Jew doesn't speak to someone before[?] he has first grabbed him by the lapel.
A Jew doesn't eat — he "grabs a bite"; he takes something to "grab" (refresh) his heart.
A Jew doesn't drink — he "grabs a glass", and sometimes "grabs beyond measure".
♦
A Jew doesn't go to play cards — he goes "to grab a hand".
A Jew doesn't put on his overcoat — he "grabs the kapote onto himself".
A Jew won't simply go for some air — he will go "to grab a bit of fresh air".
A Jew doesn't read a newspaper — he "grabs a look"; he also grabs a look into someone else's letter, into someone else's book.
A Jew doesn't sleep — he "grabs a nap"; and if he does sleep, he "grabs himself up" (wakes with a start).
A Jew loves to "grab a chat" with a scholar; as soon as one "grabs hold of him", he is "grabbed" (thrilled).
A Jew would also like to "grab his way up" the "Jungfrau", only she is a bit too high (altogether, as is established, 13 thousand[?] feet, and reckoned the third-highest mountain in Switzerland[?]). Having no choice, he grabs his way up onto the bench of pride...
A Jew has imperialist aims: he would like to grab the "brekhli"[?], the prayer-leader's lectern — not only on a yahrzeit but the whole year.
A Jew, when he looks[?] for a first-class kosher inn where one shouldn't actually need to grab anything at all, grabs... fleas.
In summer a Jew likes to dash off to the water, to grab a look at how the women bathe, and on that occasion[?] he also grabs a beating.
A Jew, if he is "caught up in the matter", sometimes grabs the maid in an embrace; and when his "so-and-so" (wife) has dashed out of the house for a minute to grab something for the household and catches him in the act — then he catches the real slap...
A Jew who has grown-up daughters says to them: my children, dash off somewhere to a dance hall — perhaps you'll catch a fellow, and there'll be a "grab" (demand) for you.
But nobody wants to snatch them up — only the [—] grabs them!
A Jew is so used to grabbing that even when he makes a move (in chess) he grabs it back.
A Jew is no bankrupt; he merely "grabs" (borrows) until he has grabbed everywhere; and then, when he has nowhere left to grab, he grabs himself across the border, so that his creditors shouldn't grab him by the throat...
On top of that he still has a complaint against you that you grab! When you eat kugel with him from one plate and he grabs as much as the poor man can grab, he shouts: what are you grabbing, what? What kind of grabbing is this? Don't grab.
A Jew, even if he is blind in both eyes, still perceives that the other one grabs. It once happened that two beggars who went from house to house, one blind and the other sighted, were eating cholent on the Sabbath at a householder's; in the middle of the meal the sighted one suddenly got a whack over the hand with the spoon from the blind one.
— Why are you hitting, you blind glutton and drunkard? — the sighted one shouted.
— Because you grab so fast — the blind one answered angrily.
— How do you know that I gr[—]? You're blind in both ey[—].
— I don't need to see at all — the blind man ex[—]ained to him — I can already feel that you grab, because when I grab like this and you keep quiet, it's a sign that you're grabbing even more than me!
Such a grabber is the Jew. He keeps grabbing nonstop, he really suffers from khaptomania; he is so used to grabbing that even in the synagogue he grabs in a "Kedushah", a chapter of Psalms, a Kaddish.
And when he has nothing left to grab, he grabs leftovers at the rebbe's table, or sits at home catching flies.
Oy, what a grabby people we are,
Municipal Taxes on Dogs, Apartments, Hotels and Signboards

[Będzin — City Council.]
[Subheading:] The 4th trade category and the 8th industry category exempted from the signboard tax.
On Monday[?] evening the City Council held a session at which a series of statutes of municipal taxes were adopted, such as on dogs, apartments, hotels and signboards, and also the plan for developing (expanding) the town.
Because of the last statute almost all the Jewish councillors came. (The article in today's issue addressed to the Jewish councillors was written under the impression of the previous City Council session.)
After the adoption of the plan, which provides for the development of the town, the first two statutes were adopted after a short discussion.
A good while was taken up by the discussion of the hotel-tax statute. Speakers: Dr. Weinzieher, Mrs. Ts. Szejn, Goldsztajn and Zylberberg, who support the request of the hotel owners that the percentage of occupied rooms be reduced to 3 per cent.
The left-wing groupings speak out against it, and it is decided that the percentage shall be at the level of 10 per cent.
The "high point" (lit. "tshak") of the session was the signboard tax. On the motion of councillor Zylberberg a recess is called. During the recess negotiations are conducted toward a compromise on the question.
As a result, the signboard tax was adopted according to the commission's draft. Exempted were only merchants holding 4th-category trade licences ("patents") and 8th-category craftsmen's licences.
Parnas Goldsztajn as a Member of the Kehilla Board

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
This week parnas Mr. L. Goldsztajn received from the starosta (district head) a notification that, on the basis of the signature[?], which Mr. G. — who at the time was on the list of candidates for the board — he enters the board as a member.
The Development of the "Discount Bank"

[Będzin — Economy.]
The "Discount Bank", which for several months has been located in the premises of the local Small Traders' Association (Małachowskiego 2), has received a new lease of life, is[?] active, and the main thing — the bank is again winning back its popular trust. The phenomenon is noticeable above all in the field of deposits (takings), which grow from week to week.
In the near future a general meeting is to take place, at which a board and a council will be elected.
Completion of a Torah Scroll at Rabbi Szapiro's

[Będzin — Religious life.]
This coming Sunday [21 February 1937] a siyum ha-sefer (celebration of the completion of a Torah scroll) will take place in the residence of the Rebbe R' Yaakov Yitzchak Szapiro (Mandushever[?] — probably Modrzejowska — 25), to which the Rebbe asks the Jewish population to take part.
A Committee of Friends of the "Zionist Lexicon" Formed

[Będzin — Zionism.]
On the model of other towns in Poland and abroad, a committee of friends of the "Zionist Lexicon" has been founded in Będzin; the Lexicon will form a complete Zionist and Eretz-Israel encyclopaedia. The committee, which includes the most prominent Zionist personalities of our town, has set itself the task of carrying out a broad subscription campaign for this monumental Zionist publication, which is edited by Dr. Y. Schiper, Dr. A. Tartakower, Dr. N. M. Gelber, M. Zwajbojm and P. Wasserman, and in which distinguished scholars and writers of all trends in Zionism collaborate.
On behalf of the "Zionist Lexicon", Mgr. G. Zwajbojm, co-editor of the Lexicon, is now staying in our town. No doubt the campaign for the Zionist encyclopaedia will meet with a warm response among the local Zionists as well as among sympathisers of Zionism.
Gordon Academy in Będzin

[Będzin — Zionism, youth movements.]
In connection with the 15th yahrzeit of A. D. Gordon, the local "Gordonia" is holding on Monday the 22nd of this month [22 February 1937] at 8 o'clock, in the hall of the "Apollo" cinema, a solemn academy (commemorative gathering) dedicated to his memory, with the participation of Dr. A. Tartakower and Y. Rabinowicz (Łódź), who will lecture on the life and work of A. D. Gordon. A rich artistic part is also planned, to be performed by the young Gordonists. The local population knows how to appreciate the merits of "Gordonia" and will surely take part in the academy in great numbers.
When Will the New Board of the Gemilut-Chesed Fund Be Called to Work?

[Będzin — interest-free loan fund.] In connection with the return from Warsaw of Mr. Sazbin [?] — representative of the "Joint" — the situation of the Gemilut-Chesed (interest-free loan) fund is becoming clearer.
Mr. Sazbin [?] is endeavouring by every possible means to smooth the way by which the new board — which includes in its composition some members and [i.e. of] the previous board, who were elected against the will of the "Joint" — may nevertheless constitute itself and take over the management of the fund's business. The efforts are [?] on the right track, and it is to be hoped that the constitution of the new board will take place in the next few days.
The interests of so important an institution, and the need of the thousands of families bound up with the fund, demand of the elected communal workers full sobriety and an objective assessment, and that they help Mr. Sazbin [?] in his sincere wish to rescue the Gemilut-Chesed fund from its threatening situation.
Sosnowiec — General Meeting of "Mizrachi" Members

[Sosnowiec — Mizrachi.] A few weeks ago things came, in the local "Mizrachi" organisation, to a "cabinet crisis". The chairman, Mr. Yitzchak Steinfeld, seeing [?] that an opposition was forming, resigned from the presidency and left the organisation without a leader.
Because of the situation thus created, a temporary committee was set up under the influence of Rabbi Hager, whose task was to bring about a general meeting.
Last Sunday the general meeting took place, chaired by Rabbi Hager.
At the meeting one could easily establish that the reason the "Mizrachi" is not at its former strength is that in the board until now the necessary harmony did not prevail, which is directly [necessary] for the strengthening of any organisation whatever. This showed itself best during the discussion, which almost bore the character of personal scores being settled.
Very weak, too, was the report of the outgoing president; it was a report on external matters — that is to say, that the "Mizrachi" was represented at conferences, conventions, etc.; on the other hand, about the internal state that the "Mizrachi" created over the last 2 years we heard nothing.
After the report, Messrs. Ziskind, Szpigel, Liberman, Karpin and Balimowski spoke; the last of them criticised the board, which had neglected the question of education, which brought about the official liquidation of the "Mizrachi" cheder.
Mr. Mintz points out that the "Mizrachi" is represented on various committees for Zionist work; especially active — he says — is Mr. W. Kożuch [?], who as a "Mizrachi" man leads almost the entire "Keren Hayesod" campaign in Sosnowiec.
The closing speech is delivered by Rabbi Hager. The speech, delivered with pathos, is an indictment of the members and [i.e. of] the "Mizrachi" who neglect "Mizrachi" interests in general and the question of education in particular.
Then Rabbi Hager reads out the persons of the new board, which, at the rabbi's request, is accepted en bloc.
With the cry "Long live the Mizrachi!" and "Hatikvah" the meeting is closed.
Purim Campaign for the Benefit of "Linas Hacholim"

[Linas Hacholim — Purim.] Tuesday's [?] meeting of the "Linas Hacholim" board was devoted to the forthcoming Purim campaign. The point was to draw the Jewish population's attention to the importance of the institution, which relieves the sufferings of the Jewish masses.
At the meeting it was decided to increase the surgery visits (consultations) for surgical illnesses to 4 days a week.
A P.K.O. Branch Office

[Banking — P.K.O.] As we wrote at the time, at the conference in the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec, with the participation of the president of Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego, Mr. Górecki, and representatives of the P.K.O. (Postal Savings Bank), it was decided to open in our town a branch office (ekspozytura) of the P.K.O.
As we learn, the head office in Warsaw has accepted the proposal, so that in the near future the branch office will be opened.
—o—
Inspector of Hebrew studies.
This week Dr. Stein, lecturer (docent) at the Jewish Institute in Warsaw, stayed in Zagłębie; he inspected the Hebrew studies in the Jewish gymnasia in Sosnowiec and in Będzin.
—o—
Ran over a pram with a child in it.
On Staszica Street a certain carter, Wieliński, driving very fast, ran over a child's pram in which there was a two-year-old child, who was seriously injured. The pram was smashed.
Guszeszalski and his wife commit suicide in Kraków.

News of the suicide of Guszeszalski and his wife, who poisoned themselves with Luminal in a hotel in Kraków, made a strong impression everywhere in Zagłębie.
Guszeszalski was already found dead; his wife was taken to hospital. Her condition is not serious and there is hope of keeping her alive.
The trial of Paweł Guszeszalski, who was accused of poisoning both his children, had dragged on for a long time. The district court sentenced him to death; Guszeszalski appealed and the appeals court acquitted him for lack of evidence. The prosecutor, however, filed a cassation; a week ago the Supreme Court upheld the prosecutor's cassation and the trial was to be heard again before the appeals court; an order was also issued to arrest Guszeszalski.
Guszeszalski was then in Kraków, where he and his wife decided to commit suicide.
On the table in the hotel he left a letter which begins with the words:
"We are going away from here, because we have had enough. What we have lived through, no human heart could have borne."
In the Aleksander "shtibl" it was "layehudim"...

As is known, a sharp dispute has arisen between the kehilla commissioner and the kashrut committee over the engagement of new ne'emanim [kashrut supervisors], who are to be on duty all day in the butcher shops.
In this connection the kashrut committee issued a leaflet directed against the kehilla commissioner.
Last Sabbath the leaflet was distributed among the worshippers in the above-mentioned "shtibl". The sons of one of the local shochtim [ritual slaughterers] reacted sharply against the distribution (the latter support the kehilla commissioner's action on the ne'emanim question), and with their protests they caused a great scandal.
Landlord kills his tenant.

In the dock of the [?] district court sat a certain Piciak, owner of a house on Stabelna [?] Street, who during a brawl murdered his tenant Kszwor [?].
The murderer was sentenced to 7 years in prison.
Hasidic Jews from Ostrowiec and Kielce arrested.

[Kielce — community and Hasidim.] In August 1936 kehilla (Jewish community) elections were held in Ostrowiec. The majority in the kehilla was won by the followers of the well-known Ostrowiec Rebbe, R' Yechezkel Halstock, a son of the old Ostrowiec Rebbe, the famous gaon and tzaddik of the generation, R' Meir Yechiel HaLevi of blessed memory. Some years ago, however, the young "Ożarów Rebbe" (as[?] he is called), Shmuel Dov Epstein, came to Ostrowiec and settled there. This young rebbe (formerly a merchant), who wants to become a member of the Ostrowiec rabbinate, managed to "recruit" a certain number of followers. These followers lodged an appeal against the elections with the supervisory authority. They want the old kehilla board, which is however badly compromised, to go on running the Ostrowiec kehilla. A fire of strife flared up between the sides. Delegations of both sides came to Kielce quite often to intervene for and against the new kehilla elections.
Recently, apparently[?], various denunciations reached the authorities. These denunciations were sent on to the public prosecutor's office, which ordered a strict investigation to be opened. One of the senior investigating officials in Kielce was specially delegated to Ostrowiec for this purpose.
As a result of the investigation some twenty-odd persons were arrested in Ostrowiec. Searches were also made at the homes of various people. Most of those detained were released. Remaining under arrest, on the other hand, are the Ostrowiec signatories[?], Messrs. R' Naftali Szpigel[?] and R' Leibish Wene[?], as well as the "Ożarów Rebbe" Epstein and the brothers Avraham and Shimsha[?] Beinerman. These 5 persons were taken to Kielce, where on Friday they were put in prison. Together with the Ostrowiec Jews mentioned, two Aleksander Hasidim from Kielce were also arrested and put in prison, Messrs. Getzel Goldgraub and Moshe Frumer, who, it is said, had wanted to intercede on behalf of the Ożarów side.
The arrested men were held until 6 in the evening, and only after candle-lighting were they released. Only the Beinerman brothers remained in custody.
Mishloach manot for the Keren Kayemet.

[Kielce — Zionism.] As every year, this year too the local Keren Kayemet (Jewish National Fund) committee is to carry out[?] the mishloach manot (Purim gifts) campaign for the Keren Kayemet during the Purim days. Delegated pairs will visit every Jewish home to ask for mishloach manot for the Jewish people, for the building of the Land of Israel.
We are sure that Jewish Kielce will receive the collectors with a friendly welcome and will give them appropriate donations for the KKL.
Winding-up meeting of the coal-campaign committee.

[Kielce — winter relief.] This week[?] the winding-up meeting of the coal-campaign committee took place in the kehilla offices. Close to a thousand families registered for coal. The most active part in the coal campaign was taken by chairman Piotrkowski, as well as Doctor M. D. Eisenberg and parnas (kehilla elder) Meir Eisenberg.
We shall give a detailed report in the next issue.
Saturday — the trial of the desecrators of the Jewish cemetery in Kielce.

[Kielce — courts.] Tomorrow, Saturday, the trial of the young hooligans St. Kory and others, who desecrated the graves and broke the tombstones in the Jewish cemetery in Kielce, takes place in the municipal court. A number of witnesses have been summoned to the trial, among others secretary Sokołowski, official M. Korngold and others. The trial has aroused great interest.
“The Zionist Lexicon”

(A Zionist and Eretz-Israel encyclopaedia)
A Zionist encyclopaedia has begun to appear in Warsaw, edited by Dr. A. Tartakower, Dr. Schiper, Dr. N. M. [printed "N. M." with final mem] Gelber, B. Ts[—]boim [?] and P. [?] Hoferman.
This encyclopaedia, entitled “The Zionist Lexicon”, will cover, in alphabetical order, the entire range of problems in the historical process of Zionism from its beginnings (the prehistory of Zionism, Hovevei Zion) to the present day. It will give a complete picture of present-day Eretz Israel and of the Zionist work of construction in all fields; it will give the biographies of all Zionist leaders, as well as of prominent Jewish and non-Jewish personalities who have rendered great services to Zionism or to the building of Eretz Israel. It will explain all the various ideologies and trends within Zionism, and will also give a [—] survey of the entire Zionist world press and of the differences between the trends.
“The Zionist Lexicon” appears weekly and will be published in 4 large illustrated volumes (10 fascicles to each volume). So far 6 fascicles have already appeared, with an abundance of Zionist, Eretz-Israel and biographical material. The last 3 fascicles form a full [?] Palestinography — geography, demography, economics, state administration, culture, history of Eretz Israel.
It is superfluous to stress the great Zionist-cultural importance of this monumental Zionist publication, which for the first time in the history of Zionist literature will assemble, in a comprehensive and exhaustive manner, the vast Zionist and Eretz-Israel material in encyclopaedic form.
In the larger cities of Poland and abroad committees of friends of the Zionist encyclopaedia have been founded, which have set themselves the task of carrying out a broad subscription campaign for this so important and topical publication.
Łódź led the way, where a special committee was founded, which the most eminent personalities have joined, headed by Dr. Markus Braude [?]. Here too a similar committee has been created.
Constituent meeting of the Zionist Committee.

This Tuesday the first constituent meeting of the Zionist Committee took place. A presidium was elected, consisting of the following members: A. Grinberg (chairman), Eng. Cukierman (vice-chairman), Dr. Poliak (vice-chairman), editor Nielani [?] (secretary) and M. Cytryn (treasurer). The new committee has already set to work.
Newspapers for the patients in the Jewish hospital.

The Magistrate has recently had boxes put up at every corner of the city, into which newspapers are dropped for the patients in the municipal hospital.
It is very desirable that the Jewish population, too, should drop Jewish newspapers into the newspaper boxes, especially for the Jewish patients who wish to read Yiddish newspapers.
The “Silnica” overflows.

The rain, from which the snow quickly melted, caused the river “Silnica” to overflow.
In the area of Pakosz Dolny the “Silnica” flooded houses, bridges and the highway. Firemen took part in the rescue.
The kehilla budget for 1937.

As we are informed, the kehilla administration will set about drawing up the budget for 1937 at the beginning of next week. The new budget will thus be drawn up by the old administration.

Left for Eretz Israel
This week Mr. S. Lewartowski left for Eretz Israel for the wedding of his daughter, which takes place on 2 March in Haifa.
A few days ago Mr. Moshe Fridman (owner of the bookshop on Bodzentyńska [?] Street) also left for Eretz Israel, as a tourist.

Mr. Kreizman’s grocery shop emptied.
Unknown persons a few days ago emptied the grocery (“colonial goods”) shop of Mr. Moshe Kreinman [?] on Post [Pocztowa?] Street. The stolen goods amount to over a thousand złoty.

Editor Dubois’s lecture in Kielce postponed
Last Sunday a lecture by the well-known PPS leader, editor Dubois, on the subject “Nationalism and Antisemitism” was to take place in the Teatr Polski. Because editor Dubois did not come, the lecture was postponed to this Sunday.

A conference.
Under the chairmanship of the Kielce voivode Dr. Dziadosz [?], a 2-day conference of the deputy starostas of the Kielce voivodeship took place in Kielce.
Mr. Slaszik [?], an inspector of the Ministry of the Interior, took part in the conference.

Jakl[?] Stachowski[?] with his companion[?] from Czeladź were charged with insulting the Polish nation. Yesterday, Thursday, the trial took place at the Sosnowiec district court. On trading hours on Saturday evening.
The trade section of the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec, having considered the proposals of the Jewish and Polish merchants' associations concerning trading hours at the close of the Sabbath (motzaei Shabbat), has come to a decision according to which all shops (except food shops) will be open only until 19.30, barbershops and flower shops no later than 21 o'clock.

A Shtetl Where Wives “Are Afraid to Take Purses with Money from Their Husbands”...

[Pilica — family life; divorce.] The shtetl of Pilica is in an uproar because of the sensational story that took place there these days.
Into the apartment of a certain woman, who has been separated from her husband for quite some time, came two[?] well-known people, local residents, who handed the woman a little purse, saying that her husband, who wishes to make peace with her again, had sent her a few złotys[?] as a token of “peace”.
The woman, believing what the people had told her, took the little purse from them, and at that moment the “angels of peace” cried out to her:
— “Here you have a get [bill of divorce], and we are the witnesses”...
It goes without saying that the side[?] of the deceived woman is seeking ways to invalidate the get, but the incident has struck such fear into the local wives that “they don't want to touch their husbands' money-purses”...
Who Can Obtain Craftsman's Cards in the New Trades

[Poland — crafts and regulations.] In connection with the fact that a whole series of trades have recently been classed as crafts, the United Committee for Jewish Crafts Affairs explains that the persons concerned who were 21 years old before 30 June 1936 and who before that date (i.e. before 30 June 1936) had notified the Industry Office that they run a workshop (millinery[?], corset-making[?], linen-sewing[?] etc.) can obtain a craftsman's card, using the confirmation of their notification („poświadczenie zgłoszenia“[?]) for a craftsman's card.
Those who hold a trade licence (patent) taken out for the 1st half of 1936, or receipts for turnover tax or signboard tax, must apply with a request to the Chamber of Crafts for the issue of a confirmation that they possess acquired rights. After receiving this confirmation they must apply to the starostwo (district office) for the issue of a craftsman's card to them.
All those who do not possess the documents mentioned must obtain from the magistrate (municipality) a certificate that before 30 June 1936 they ran an independent workshop in the new trade. With this certificate and a proper request they must apply to the appropriate Chamber of Crafts.

[Będzin — Betar; Trumpeldor.] At the Będzin Betar branch (ken) on Sunday evening a ceremonial mourning assembly (roll-call) took place in memory of the 17th yahrzeit of Joseph Trumpeldor, with the participation of the commissioner's officer Mgr. M. Begin[?] [probably Menachem Begin].

What's Happening in Upper Silesia? — The Budget of the Katowice Kehilla

In the office of the kehilla in Katowice the kehilla budget for the year 1937 has been laid out for inspection by the payers of the community tax (etat)[?]. The budget amounts to a sum of 661 thousand zł., which are also foreseen in the revenues. Compared with last year, this year's budget is higher by about 200 thousand zł., which have been earmarked for the new kehilla building.
