Paris Notes

[Paris — letter from Paris; the World Exhibition; French Jewry; Będzin natives in Paris.] (From our Paris correspondent)
From the Exhibition.
The Paris International Exhibition, which has been crowned with the title „Art and Technology“, takes on a broader scope with every day; its success is enormous. The 42 nations taking part in it have sought by every possible means to outdo one another; each nation has brought here its finest and best wonders in order to show the world its history, inventions, art and technology. We Jews, too, need not be ashamed of the splendid Palestine pavilion — executed by talented Palestinian [i.e. Eretz-Israel] architects. I shall come back specially to its architecture and interior arrangement. Another pavilion, of modern Jewish culture, is also now being built, which will be finished and opened within the next few days. The organising committee consists of such artists as: Einhorn [David Einhorn], Charney [Daniel Charney], Shneour [Zalman Shneour], Mané-Katz, Wiewiórka [Abraham Wiewiórka] and others, which promises us that it will be of the highest artistic and literary value. Care is also being taken that the pavilion should bear a specially Jewish style.
How great the success of the exhibition is can be seen from the entrance tickets, which are registered automatically: if in the first days 80 to 90 thousand visitors a day were recorded, it has already grown[?] — on Sunday 27 June 264 thousand entrance tickets were officially registered for that Sunday alone, and this is still only the beginning, because not all the pavilions are open yet.
The exhibition is visited by all classes and strata of the population. Strolling through the exhibition last week, I met a Jewish rebbe dressed in a satin kapote and a broad rabbinical hat, and talking with him I actually learned that he is a [—][?] — a Zagłębie man.. He explained to me that, being in Paris on account of other matters, he does not want to miss the opportunity of visiting the exhibition.
Jewishness.
If before the Popular Front government came to power Jewishness in France stood on a low level, under the government of Léon Blum it has become extraordinarily pious. As you know, among the other social laws the government adopted, the 40-hour working week was also established, with 2 days of rest — Saturday and Sunday; jesters see in this a hint of redemption... For if formerly on the Sabbath the Jewish synagogues were [—][?] and one always had to wait for a minyan, since Léon Blum decreed[?] the Sabbath rest one can no longer find a place in the synagogues on the Sabbath, and the gabbaim, cantors and beadles only now know what life is... and they praise the government to high heaven and wish it length of days. Even our Paris shochtim — our klei kodesh — have become ardent adherents of the Popular Front and, in recognition, have joined the C.G.T., i.e. the French workers' syndicate, and will wage[?] the class struggle with all their might[?] together with them; and people even say that they will have to go twice a week to Léon Jouhaux (a Christian) — the president of the syndicates — to have him inspect the slaughter-knives, lest, God forbid, they have a nick and thereby cause the Jewish householders to stumble into non-kosher slaughter..
In the Bendiner „Society“.
In our Paris „Bendiner Society“ [society of Będzin natives] some changes have recently taken place in the leadership of the committee. The old board, which had existed for several months without any active work, convened after Léon Blum's resignation and also decided to resign... Most of the members, surprised and at the same time pleased with the decision, elected in its place a new board, in which we find the names of our most active members, such as Arnaldicz[?], Perec, Wicenberg[?], Muszyński, Gutberger and others.
At the first general meeting called by the board it was decided, among other things, to send several[?] of the members' children on vacation, even to the seaside; [to give] a subsidy of 300[?] francs to the relief committee for Polish children, 500 francs to the committee for the victims of the anti-Jewish outbreaks and 400 francs for the Jewish children[?] in Będzin. We hereby express our wish that the present committee continue its fruitful work, begun for the benefit of its members, and that from time to time it should also not forget the needy in the old home.
Salomon Lewkowicz.
Madness and Records

[From the world — curiosities; records.] Today we hear again of a list of records that have been set recently, and of which we do not know whether we are dealing with normal people or with plain lunatics; let the facts speak for themselves. No comments are needed.
In Guni[?], a village in Yugoslavia, a 97-year-old peasant has now married for the 18th time. Of his previous 17 wives two died, and from 15 he was divorced. Since he is a rich peasant, he gives each wife a house of her own at the divorce. In the whole village there are no more than these fifteen houses, in which his divorcées live, most of them already with other husbands...
The old fellow wishes to live to a hundred — by then he will have married his twentieth wife... The newspapers present this item as a „record in marrying“...
And[?] another record: in the Vienna Prater two sisters can now be seen. The younger is 19 years old and weighs 208 kilos, the elder is 22 years old and weighs 285 kilos. A further „record“ is set there by a 17-year-old Hungarian girl who is 2 metres 65 centimetres tall..
In Vienna the wife of an unemployed[?] „tapliar“[?] (upholsterer?) has set a „record“: she has now given birth to her 21st child; in honour of the great „record“ the husband has now received a post in a municipal enterprise.
At the Leipzig fair one could see a Negro, the greatest glutton. His lunch[?], which he ate every day, consisted of: two large meat schnitzels, 120 eggs, a lot of lemons, twenty kilos of fruit, and on top of that he drank a hundred bottles of soda water.
This „record eater“ told that only once did he upset his stomach, when he won the bet that he would eat four large spoons of cement dissolved in water... At that time he had several days of stomach-ache, but money changed hands and he went on eating „once more“.
Once in America he won a bet of a thousand dollars; he ate at one go 24 raw eggs with the shells...
In America he was once a blood donor. The doctors found that his blood was very good against all kinds of diseases. In all he gave his blood for 748 patients over eight years, i.e. twice every week. But in that time he had to „eat better“, and he put on forty kilos. Then the doctors stopped taking him, because there was already too much fat in his blood, so he took up again setting records in the laws of eating...
In one of the finest clubs in London a record in drinking has been set. The club has two hundred members, and in the last 25 years they have drunk 470 thousand litres of fine port wine, three hundred thousand barrels of beer, two thousand tons of liqueur, and they have smoked five hundred tons of cigars.
As Indian papers report, records in eating have begun to be set there too. One of the Indian princes celebrated the 25th anniversary of his reign; for it he invited his hundred thousand subjects and had ten thousand oxen and ten thousand sheep slaughtered for the feast. Ten people had to eat a whole ox and a whole sheep at one meal...
How many subjects may upset their stomachs over it, the papers there do not say...
Z. Haber, Vienna.
From the Book Table.

[Book review — Jewish economics; YIVO.] “Di yidishe ekonomik” (Jewish Economics), a monthly journal, No. 1, May 1937, published by the Economic-Statistical Section of “YIVO”, edited by J. Leshchinsky (Jakub Leszczyński).
The journal has published articles “on Jewish sociological, economic and statistical questions; statistical notes on: biotics[?] (vital statistics), economics, culture, criminology; bibliography”.
(“Our Tasks and Aims”).
Among all peoples the whole life of the country is regulated by the state, more or less, in every respect, and there is “an eye that sees”: in the statistical offices they weigh and measure the entire economic structure of the country, and science is used entirely for this purpose. It is enough to take as an example America under Roosevelt’s rule, with his “Brain Trust” of social scientists, which rescued the country from a terrible crisis; whereas with us Jews everything is neglected in the field of planning[?] research, and we live “without reckoning”, and as the folk saying goes: “If you live without reckoning, you die without confession.” And therefore it is no wonder that we see a sad phenomenon: Jewish trade in the small town is being pushed out and gradually liquidated (the article by Jakub Leshchinsky), because the Jewish merchant and petty trader are not properly organized, and there is no organized institution that would stand on watch and come to their aid with advice and deed; in general chaos reigns in Jewish economic life — and this is happening at a time of “a general upheaval in Jewish destiny, which is the result of a world overturn[?], in which mankind has been confronted with the fundamental question of rebuilding all the foundations of life”.
And therefore the undertaking of “YIVO” in Vilna (Wilno) deserves to be welcomed, which has set about publishing the journal “Di yidishe ekonomik”, which is to be “an instrument that will help the Jewish masses find their way in the tangle of processes spreading through[?] Jewish life”.
The Jewish street must support this periodical, so that a serious forum for Jewish economics may be created.
In conclusion we would like to remark on J. Leshchinsky’s article on “Jewish trade” that it would be worthwhile to undertake a study of the migration from the small towns to the larger cities, and especially to the industrial centres of Zagłębie and Upper Silesia; this would provide a great deal of illuminating material on the problem.
Very interesting notes are given in the journal on Jewish emigration to Palestine (Eretz Israel), from which we learn that Palestine occupies 6th place, right below the Jewish communities in Hungary and Germany.
Elchanan Zyder.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Matot-Masei)

[Oneg Shabbat — weekly Torah portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Matot-Masei
—o—
a) “Avenge the vengeance of the children of Israel” (31:2)
It does not say “avenge the vengeance of the Lord”, because the Midianites[?] too said that they were avengers of the Lord’s vengeance, that they wished to exterminate the Jews in the name of God. Have few people been murdered in the name of God?..
Imrei Chen.
• • •
Of the holy man of Slavuta, R’ Shmuel Abba Shapira, another good saying is told:
In the Yotzer hymn for Parashat Zakhor the following words are found: “May his name and memory be blotted out, and may he be erased from being mentioned in holy remembrance.” What do these words mean?
Why, Amalek too was surely a “saint” among the Jew-hating nations; they surely spoke of him as of a saint who did so much to exterminate the dreadful Jewish race — that is the meaning of “may he be erased from being mentioned in holy remembrance”: that his memory as a saint should be wiped out...
b) “And you shall be guiltless before the Lord and before Israel” (32:22)
“A person must satisfy his obligations to people just as he must satisfy his obligations to God, as it is said: And you shall be guiltless before the Lord and before Israel.” (Shekalim ch. 3, mishnah 2.)
R’ Israel Salanter said about this: “A person must satisfy his obligations to people just as he must satisfy his obligations to God” — “just as” (ke-derekh): in the same way in which one fulfils one’s duty toward God, one should fulfil it toward people too; for most often people wish to please others through bad qualities — most often bad qualities are a way of winning favour with people. This is what the Mishnah says: to please people one must go the same way, “ke-derekh”, as one pleases God, that is, through elevated and good qualities...
• • •
First “before the Lord” and only then “before Israel”: first one must find favour with God, one must be at peace with one’s own conscience, and then one is automatically at peace with people too; for once one has a clean conscience, one need not fear all sorts of human gossip...
R’ Azariah Figo.
c) “Build you cities for your little ones, and folds for your sheep, and do that which has proceeded out of your mouth” (ibid., 24)
The Amshinover[?] Rebbe had run up heavy debts building a villa in Otwock, and he said:
Now I understand why it is said: “Build you cities for your little ones, and folds for your sons[?], and do that which has proceeded out of your mouth.” What connection does the verse have? How does building towns come together with the command that a person should keep his word? It must be that in building one runs up so many debts that it then becomes hard to keep one’s word..
d) “And Moses wrote their goings out according to their journeys by the commandment of the Lord.”
Moses recorded all the wanderings that the Jews made by the commandment of the Lord, by God’s order; but those wanderings that the Jews would have to make by the orders of strangers — those Moses was not able to record in one portion, nor even in one Torah...
Likutei Chaveri.
e) “This is the land that shall fall unto you for an inheritance” (34:2)
“Lacking space.” Yalkut.
What does the Yalkut mean by this? Why, the Midrash says: “It is called the Land of the Deer (Eretz Tzvi), etc.” — that the Land of Israel was shrunken and after the lot it expanded. Now it has shrunk again, and in the future it will be so wide that it will take in all the Jews.
That is what the Yalkut means by “lacking space”: until now there was a lack of room, and after the lot it was widened...
R’ Hirsh Melech of Dynów.
• • •
When R’ Hirsh Henech (Tzvi Hanoch) of blessed memory, the Rabbi of Będzin, was in the Land of Israel, he marvelled at the remarkable natural phenomenon there: that between the climate of one town and the next there is an enormous difference. Where does this come from?
He answered:
“It is called the Land of the Deer, etc.” — because the Land of Israel was once much wider than it is today, but it shrank; it follows that from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem there is in truth such a distance as justifies the great change of climate...
f) “Until the death of the high priest” (35:25)
What is the sense of it, that with the death of the high priest the unintentional offenders in the cities of refuge should be set free?
Because after the death of the high priest another one was of course elected, so an amnesty was granted to all the unintentional offenders in the cities of refuge — just as when a king ascends the throne, an amnesty is granted to all offenders...
Don Isaac Abravanel.
A. Zaglembier — The Living Corpse (16)

[Literature — serial novel ("The Living Corpse"), instalment 16.]
A. Zaglembier [pen name].
(A most thrilling novel of Jewish life in Zagłębie before and during the World War). (16
— But I've already told you, you want to make me unhappy and perhaps bring misfortune on yourself as well..
— No, Yaski, I want the two of us, you and I, both to be happy.. You know how much I love you; without you I won't be able to live...
— I love you too, believe me, Hanka, but it's impossible! Just think what could come of it..
— Nothing can come of it. I've told you more than once: if you don't want to become a [convert?], then I'll become a Jewess.. I'll go to the rabbi, we'll go away to another town, far from here, and you'll divorce your wife — with you people that's easy to do...
— Think it over, Hanka — says Yasl, and all the while his blood is boiling — think it over, it's not nearly as easy as you think... Listen to me, Hanka, you'll see that it will be better the way I say..
— What?..
— You already know. Go over the border to Katowice. I'll go with you if you don't want to go alone; here, look, I've brought you a few hundred roubles — everything I own; well, take it and go over to the doctor...
But at that moment all of Hanka's gentleness vanished; she grew very angry, and looking at Yasl with furious [?], glowing eyes, she pushed away his hand with the money and cried:
— No! No! I won't do it! You're a Jew, you go [?] about it the sly way! I know what you're after — you want to be rid of me, Yazu [?].
— No, Hanka! I swear to you!..
— You swear falsely! Get away from me! I know you well by now! That's why you want no trace to remain!
— Hanka, why shout? Believe me...
— I don't want to believe you, if you've dug your heels in like that.
— But I want [?] you to understand, Hanka...
— And why don't you want to understand me? Because I love you? Because I gave myself to you?..
— It will be easier for you too; people will point their fingers at you, saying you had a bastard, a love-child..
— Don't let that bother you! Leave the shame to me — but you won't deny that you're the father!
— But what good is it to you, when you can avoid all this in a good way... Come on, Hanka, take the money, listen to me...
Now Hanka boiled over completely; she pushed him away from her again, started cursing, and running off from him she said:
— I'll do as I see fit, and you do as you please!
With these words Hanka ran off alone, leaving Yasl alone in the forest.
And neither of them knew that their conversation had been overheard by a third person, "Szmulek Łapka", who was lying hidden among the trees..
For the first moment Yasl stood there with a jumble in his head. Not knowing what was happening to him, he shouted after Hanka, called her back; but she, full of anger and resentment, did not look back again and ran back into town, home. And then on the way she ran into none other than pock-marked Wacek [?].
And only now did the danger grow in Yasl's eyes, with all its terrible consequences..
And what would he really do when Hanka brought a bastard into his house and said: "Here, this is your child"!.. He already knows [?] in advance what will happen then: his wife will have a fit of hysteria [?]; weak as she is [?], she will surely not withstand it, and the children [—]... And how will he look in town.. He'll be left without a livelihood. Who will want him? Oh God! Why didn't he know all this before he let himself be drawn into the net?..
Still, he thinks, he will try every means to prevent the disaster, and as a first step he decided to go over to Hanka's parents. He will speak to them openly and plainly; Hanka's father is a decent man, an honest Christian; perhaps he himself won't want to bring such shame upon himself.
And Yasl is already about to go back into town. But at that moment his heart gave a jolt as he suddenly heard a suspicious rustle beside him. He spun round abruptly and was left even more terrified, seeing a pair of human, glittering, murderous eyes fixed upon him.
In a choked [?] voice, full of dread, Yasl cried out:
— Who's there?!
In a single moment "Szmulek Łapka" crawled out of his hiding place, ran up to Yasl and smiled in brotherly fashion:
— You know me quite well, Yaselé, don't you? Just take a good look at me.. I heard everything you were saying to that shiksa girl... But don't be afraid, brother, I won't "squeal" [?] on you...
At the sight of the figure Yasl stood even more frozen with fear.. "Szmulek Łapka"! The dangerous bandit! How does he come to be here?! "Łapka" is sitting in prison!..
As children the two of them had played together. "Łapka" had respectable, solid parents, and he himself had also been a decent boy, but later he fell in with bad company, and from then on their paths parted. And the older they grew, the more estranged they became. And now blind fate had brought them together again and arranged it so that the bandit of all people should know Yasl's terrible secret...
— Is it you, "Łapka"? — asks Yasl after a while, as if he could not believe his own eyes and ears.
— Who else? Don't you recognise me? Let them [?] sit in prison who knows how long — I came out today for a "stroll" in freedom. Remember, don't you dare "squeal" [?] on me, God forbid; they're surely searching for me already. I lay down here to rest a little, and you came along with your female... A pity I'm in a hurry, she'd be worth a sin... So remember, Yasl: you saw nothing and heard nothing, and now hand over those few hundred roubles — I really am without a penny. That's the only reason I showed myself to you...
— I have no money — Yasl answers instinctively.
— Eh, Yaselé Wertheim — the thief edges closer to him — "Łapka" has a good ear; I saw and heard everything. Hand over those few hundred roubles you held out to the shiksa girl; come on, one-two, I've got no time!
— I have no money — Yasl Wertheim repeats again, edges a little away from him, and marvels himself at his own boldness in the face of the dangerous bandit.
— Shall I search you?
— Don't you believe me?
— Are you giving it nicely? If not.. remember, Yasl. Don't make me angry!
Yasl might perhaps have handed him the few hundred roubles without a single superfluous word — one is not born with money, and it is not for money that one is lost. But he was afraid of something else. "Łapka" already knows the secret... He will always be able to hold him in fear, he will always be able to blackmail him. Who knows what the bandit would demand of him a second time — and so he did not want to show him the way the first time.
— Let me go — says Yasl — I swear to you I won't say anything..
— Hand over the money and you can go.
— It isn't mine.
— Never mind; you'll say "Łapka" took it from you, but say it only tomorrow. Come on, hand it over, before...
Yasl made a movement as if he were about to take the money out of his pocket, but suddenly something lifted him from the spot, and abruptly he hurled himself among the dense trees and started to run..

The Beach

[Humour and satire — "Der Kokh-Lefl" (The Cooking Ladle): a poem about the beach; followed by a joke.]
[Section heading:] "Der Kokh-Lefl" (The Cooking Ladle).

The Beach [plaża].

And here you see a man and wife,
with the child too in the middle,
they've brought the cholent along
and eat with appetite.

And worn-out bachelors,
idlers by profession,
are frequent[?] visitors here,
witnesses who catch[?] a glimpse of the body...

Since the body is burnt
and the skin just like soot,
they must hold by the [?]:
"After a fire you smell smoke."

Of dates [randki], dates without number
[?] arranged[?],
that Sabbath spent —
[?]

That is how the youth spends
the crowded[?] Sabbath — packed in[?],
the beach is a magnet[?],
it has [?], it has power[?]...

And when the sun is already setting,
her "umene"[?] already broken[?] —
the young folk go home
[?] from the [?]...

One barely gets into the house[?]
hungry as the wolves,
with the words on one's lips:
Mama, dear, help quickly.

Having eaten, having drunk,
and caught a nap besides,
only a rare[?] soul sits at home
when the sky is full of stars.

At once one grabs a bowl of water —
a pity to lose the time —
and after a day of [?] rinsing oneself
one starts[?] washing, smearing again...

Having eaten, washed up,
dressed — ah, one is delighted!
In company one marches straight to the shore,
it is bliss — what more[?] [could one want] in the world.

The Unhappy Husband, Poor Thing!

[Humour and satire — "Der Kokh-Lefl": a satirical conversation.]
A conversation between "straw widowers" [słomiani wdowcy — men whose wives are away on holiday].

In a local restaurant we overheard a conversation between two "straw widowers" ["slomiane hrozbes"[?]]; one of them complained:
— My neighbour Zelig[?] Higertrank[?] is, poor thing, an unhappy man. He has a wife whom he hates, but she loves him like life itself, she is as faithful to him as a slave, cooks well and bakes well and is a great [?] ["aynbrangerin"]. If she were at least ugly, false, a nobody, he would have an excuse not to live with her, and perhaps he would bring it to a divorce. But he has no luck, poor thing, that unhappy neighbour of mine. As it happens she is a beauty, a great housewife and very faithful — go and divorce such a wife! How can one obtain a divorce when the wife is so nice, so decent, so faithful?
So my neighbour, poor thing, is unhappy for his whole life!
When a "9-er" Travels to Krynica

[Humour and satire — "Der Kokh-Lefl": Będzin — a satirical travelogue; to be continued.]
A travel account for the "Kokh-Lefl".

One of the Będzin "9-er" Hasidim travelled to Krynica these days and sent the "Kokh-Lefl" his travel impressions; we reproduce only a part. Here is what he writes:
...In short, I said the "Asher yatsar" blessing and slowly [pomału] opened the carriage door of the second class. On the bench I saw a woman sitting with a suitcase [czemodan], reading a newspaper.
I wrestled with the question: go in?
Not go in?
The good inclination [?] into my ear:
— Fie, [?] fie! It is not proper[?] for you to be alone with a strange woman.
But at once the evil inclination [?] to me:
— Psst... don't be a [?]; one eats[?] there, well, [?] still Shmelke[?]...
Finally I took the handkerchief out of my trouser pocket and tied knots [to cast lots].
It came out: yes, go in.
— Oh well [mniejsza], I thought to myself, I can see plainly that it is fated — so I opened the door and in I went in peace. At first I felt very uncomfortable [przykro] being alone [sam na sam] with a married woman, so I turned away with my... face to my own side, and sitting turned like that I saw — oh, what I saw! May my eyes never see such things again, dear Father in Heaven.
On her hands she had [?] a full manicure, the silk blouse [bluzka] was cut low down to — —.

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: Hooligan Outbreaks Are Suppressed by the Police

[Head of the local page; Będzin — anti-Jewish violence, police.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 1 Av 5697 — piątek 9 lipca 937 [Friday, 9 July (1)937].)
Będzin
Hooligan outbreaks are suppressed by the police.
As we have already written, on Wednesday evening several Jewish and non-Jewish rowdies ("awanturnicy") fought one another, of whom 3 persons (2 Christians and 1 Jew) were taken to the municipal hospital. The incident, however, was exploited by dark elements, who prepared to stage a rampage ("hulanka") throughout the town.
In the course of Thursday various rumours circulated, which aroused alarm among the Jewish population. Later, at about 6 in the evening, the rumours were confirmed: from every corner of the town unfamiliar faces appeared, who began to gather on Kołłątaja Street, but thanks to the energetic intervention of the police the mob was dispersed. Many had their papers checked and the suspects were promptly detained, and only thanks to the vigilance of the supervising authority [?] did no serious outbreaks take place. In the town only a certain number of windowpanes were smashed. The incited mob, which was not let into the town, ran riot a little in the suburbs and caused great damage, for example in Gzichów, at Łask's [?], Hellner's [?], Kanał's [?] and others. In the orphanage on Sienkiewicza Street more than 50 windowpanes were smashed, in the S. Fürstenberg Gymnasium over 70 panes; the windowpanes were also smashed in the Jewish homes on Krakowska Street and in Ksawera. There were also cases in which Christian house-owners defended the Jewish tenants in the suburbs and drove off the hooligans. Such a case also occurred when a gang threw stones from the "Góra Zamkowa" (Castle Hill) at the building of "Linat ha-Holim": a neighbouring Christian house-owner then came out and drove off the attackers.
At the same time in Dąbrowa, too, a dark mob wanted to "have some fun" and began breaking into Jewish shops, but the police were soon on the spot and restored order.
From the Committee for Brisk

[Będzin — relief, anti-Jewish violence.]
Under the chairmanship of the president Mr. S. Fürstenberg, a meeting of the Relief Committee for Brisk [Brześć] took place on Tuesday evening [?]. According to the report given at the meeting, it turns out that up to the present day 4,500 zł. have been collected in our town.
At the meeting there was a delegation from Gzichów, which asked for support for the families whose windowpanes were smashed in the night to Friday.
Before His Death He Had Himself Nicely Shaved

[Będzin — suicide.]
In the night to Wednesday the caretaker ("stróż") of the house at Kołłątaja 46 hanged himself. A day earlier he went into Rudolf's [?] "rezure" [?] and demanded that they shave him nicely.
'Come Back to Us' — Christian Residents Tell a Jewish Family

[Będzin — Jewish–Christian relations.]
Binyamin Erlich lives in Ksawera; he also has a shop there. Recently it happened several times that hooligans took goods from him and would not pay, and in general threatened [?] him, so out of fear he packed up all his belongings and on Friday evening moved over with his family to his brother-in-law Yanke [?] Fridman.
But already the next morning several Christian neighbours came and asked Erlich to come back to Ksawera: "God forbid, nothing will happen to you; we will guard you from all harm."
How far good relations prevail between Erlich and his Christian neighbours is shown by the following fact:
One of the Christian women, on coming into Fridman's apartment, fell upon Erlich's wife and kissed her warmly.
Erlich, moved by such sincerity, went back to Ksawera.
Alms-Collector Accuses a Kehilla Official of Insulting Polish Decorations

[Będzin — Kehilla, police.]
In the secretariat of the local kehilla the following incident occurred last Monday:
A Jewish alms-collector, a certain Dorf, who had come into the kehilla for a donation, would not accept the 50 gr. which the cashier had given him, but demanded a larger donation. When the person began to talk in a louder tone, the official Mr. Brakiewicz [?] pointed out to him that he should behave more quietly and not make scenes.
Dorf then went out and soon came back with a policeman, to whom he declared that Bradkiewicz [?] had used insulting words about the war decorations which he wears.
On the basis of this declaration a police report was drawn up against Bradkiewicz [?].
1,800 zł. for the Half-Colony for Jewish Children

[Będzin — municipality, children.]
At a meeting of the town board it was resolved to allocate a sum of 1,800 zł. to the half-colony (day summer camp) for Jewish children.

Commission elected to audit the activity of the commissarial kehilla board — First meeting of the kehilla council. — Declarations of all groupings. — The first task is to elect a rabbi. — A budget commission elected.

Last Sunday afternoon the first meeting of the local kehilla council [in Sosnowiec] took place. The meeting aroused due interest; present were all the councillors (parnassim), almost the entire kehilla board and a numerous gallery. The first meeting of our „parliament“ stood under the impression of the newly created Jewish state, and indeed each[?] group came out with its „Ani Maamin“ (credo) about the tasks of the kehilla — fine principal[?] ideas. But councillor Mr. Dalisman is a practical man, so he declared that everything is vanity of vanities[?]; only the rabbinate question is the essence of the kehilla...
—
On the agenda: purchase of a plot for a cemetery, and the budget for the year 1937. The chairman (president) Mr. Meitlis opens the meeting with the agenda and reads a declaration in which he stresses that he will not favour any party whatsoever; his work in the kehilla will be for the whole Jewish population.
Dr. H. Liberman protests that this[?] meeting was called for last Sunday[?] afternoon and proposes that from now on the council meetings be called for 7 o'clock onward and be open[?] to everyone; then Dr. Liberman reads a declaration on behalf of his group!
Dr. Melodysta[?] supports the proposal concerning the time of the meetings; he also proposes electing a commission to examine the activity of the commissarial (government-appointed) kehilla board. On behalf of the National Bloc Dr. Melodysta reads a declaration.
Over Dr. Melodysta's proposal a discussion develops, during which a sharp exchange of words takes place between Dr. [name missing in print] and the chairman, who would not agree that one demand[?] of Dr. Melodysta that the proposal of councillor A. Liberman — to include[?] it in the agenda — be put to a vote a second time. „If you don't like it — President Meitlis said to Dr. Melodysta — you can leave.“ To this Dr. Melodysta replied: „I will not leave this place, but if you conduct things this way, you will be led out of here.“
The incident was settled when Liberman's proposal was put to the vote and was defeated.
Councillor Sycemski[?] speaks against Dr. Melodysta's proposal: if we audit the activity of the commissarial kehilla board, then the activity of the previous kehilla board should be audited as well.
Councillor Shlomo Dalisman declares on behalf of his group (Englard[?]), which — he says — received the largest number of votes in the kehilla elections, that the first task of the kehilla is to settle the rabbinate question. If the rabbinate question is not settled, kehilla activity will remain stuck at a dead point.
Councillor Ruszekowicz[?]: it is chutzpah to say that the rabbinate question is the essence of the kehilla; the rabbinate question is no more than one little link in the general chain of the kehilla. Our task is to work for the matters that concern the whole community.
The same opinion is voiced by Vice-President Mr. Jasny, who proposes honouring the deceased Nahum Sokolow, Dr. Kohn, Rezau[?] and board member Weissbach[?]. Mr. Jasny reads a declaration on behalf of the Revisionist organisation.
Councillor Goldberg (Right Poalei Zion), before reading his declaration, proposes honouring by rising the fallen martyrs (kedoshim) in Eretz Israel and in the Diaspora.
Then the votes on the above-mentioned proposals take place. Dr. Liberman's proposal concerning the time of the meetings is adopted. A longer discussion takes place over the proposal to elect an audit commission, and it is resolved that such a commission be created; but if it turns out that it is necessary also to audit the activity of the last kehilla board, that shall be done.
The audit commission is joined[?] by: Dr. Melodysta, Sycemski, S. Dalichman[?], J. Goldberg, Dr. Liberman, B. Wszenmkowicz[?], D. Dzukiewicz[?].
On the first item of the agenda, buying a plot, the kehilla president Lejzerowicz reports, and he declares that 3 members of the council must also be elected to the purchase commission. The declaration is taken note of, and Messrs. Meitlis, Sycemski and Ratner[?] are elected.
On the budget item, Dr. Liberman's proposal is adopted to elect a budget commission, which is to acquaint itself with the draft budget and later present it to the plenum. Elected to the budget commission: Dr. Liberman, Sycemski, Dalisman, Diament and Wszemkowicz[?]. With that the meeting was closed.
A Halutzim Patronage Elected

On the initiative of the kehilla president Mr. Lejzerowicz, a meeting took place in the kehilla premises with the participation of a number of public and national activists of our town [Sosnowiec].
The chairman Mr. Lejzerowicz explains that the aim of the gathering is to create a patronage that will be the actual guardian (apotropos) of the halutz kibbutzim in and around Sosnowiec.
After a short discussion the following patronage was elected: Rabbi Hager, President Józef Safer[?], Eng. Weigryb[?], Mrs. Dr. Kozalska[?], Dr. [Dr.] Melodysta[?], Dr. Zybersztański[?], W. Kanszuk[?], H. Stachski[?], councillor Goldberg, M. Langman, R. Skrzynia[?], A. Chlebnicki[?], representatives of „Gordonia“ and „Hashomer Hatzair“, and Dr. Golbard[?].
Activity of the Brześć (Brisk) Committee in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — Relief for the Brześć victims.]
The Brześć (Brisk) Committee in Sosnowiec announces:
The collection campaign, which has been conducted up to now, has brought in the sum of 8,328.96 zł. for the Central Committee in Warsaw, and 8,000 zł. have been transferred.
The communiqué of the Central Committee that recently appeared in the press emphasises that Sosnowiec occupies, among the 80 towns that have so far sent money to Warsaw, one of the most honourable places — fourth place.
At the same time the committee emphasises that there are very rich persons who have not yet fulfilled their duty towards the stricken Jews of Brześć; their names will later be published in the press.
The committee appeals to all Jews who have not yet fulfilled their duty not to wait for the visits of the money-collectors, but to bring their donations at once to the cash office of the Jewish kehilla board.

A Hooligan Deed.
On First of May Street (ul. 1 Maja) several young hooligans beat up 13-year-old Gutshe (Gucia) Flojm, who was taken to the Jewish hospital, where it was established that one of her eyes too had been badly hurt by the blows.

Drunkards Cause a Panic.
On Dekerta Street two drunkards accosted Jewish passers-by, which caused something of a panic. The police who arrived put an end to the row, and it became quiet.

What Thieves Are..
A burglary was committed in the flat of the vice-president of the local district court. The thieves broke the locks of the flat, from where they stole 800 zł. in cash, as well as bonds of the Investment Loan.
These Are Your Leaders, Kielce!...

„Life in Kielce“ — Friday, 1 Av 5697 — piątek 9 lipca 1937 [Friday, 9 July 1937].
Soon after the events in Brisk [Brześć], we pointed out the regrettable fact that the appointed Jewish institutions in Kielce had not undertaken any collection campaign [?].
We were fully convinced that if [?] an aid committee were created, and as soon as the campaign began, there was not the slightest doubt that the campaign would be crowned with the greatest success.
We did not find it necessary to write special agitation articles for the campaign.
Still less could we have reckoned that we would have to dun [?] the Jewish public for the ruin [?]. How could that ever have entered one's mind?!
To our greatest regret we are deeply disappointed in the moral and social maturity and elementary sense of responsibility of Jewish Kielce!
Deeply disappointed are we. We did not expect such social decline, such immaturity and such irresponsibility!
One's face simply bursts with shame that such a "mother-city in Israel" as Kielce has to this day not given a single penny for Brisk!
And greater still is the disgrace that when a meeting was called on the matter of Brisk, out of a hundred invited people barely 10 (ten) came. The rest did not deign to come. Had it been a question of a „meg-kli'“ [?] in the kehilla, the city council or elsewhere, then all the prestige-hungry [?] "cooking-ladles" [busybodies] would have turned up as one man, and nobody would have been missing. But at the said meeting (the first and the last) no heroes were in evidence [?], and [—] nobody came.
Shame on you, Kielce! Be ashamed of your public workers, as well as of your upstart war-rich!
These are your leaders, Kielce!..

Rota of lunches for the Kielce old-age home.

Newly elected dozors and parnasim take over the management of the kehilla.
On Sunday the 11th of this month a plenary session of the newly elected dozors [kehilla board members] and parnasim will take place; on that same day they will take over the management of the Kielce kehilla.
The Committee for a Jewish Gymnasium Building at Work.

The committee for a building for Jewish schools in Kielce is calling a meeting in the next few days, at which the plans for the further collection campaign will be worked out [?]. So far — as we have already reported — only a few persons from the university-educated intelligentsia have contributed. It is to be expected that all strata of the Jewish population of Kielce will help this cause by all possible means, especially the Jewish merchant and artisan classes, who feel the necessity of creating commercial and trade schools for the young Jewish generation. In these circles it is also understood that from the moment Kielce has its own Jewish public schools, parents will no longer be so heavily burdened materially in giving their children an education.
The head of the building committee, Dr. Felc, stated in a conversation with our correspondent that the question of the site for the building will be [printed "is"] finally settled within the next few days. The site is on Mlinarska [Młynarska?] Street, in a quiet, airy neighbourhood. It is the committee's wish to proceed as quickly as possible to laying the foundation stone of the building; naturally all this depends to a great extent on the assistance of Jewish society. The committee will also turn to our Kielce landsleit abroad, asking them to take part in the campaign and help ensure that Kielce does not lag behind other Jewish communities in Poland in this respect.
On the whole, the initiators of the campaign are very optimistic and believe that the work undertaken will be crowned with success.

18 thousand złoty stolen from the Jędrzejów brewery.
From the Jędrzejów beer factory, which belongs to Mr. Eli' Szpigler, unknown persons stole a cash box from the office containing a sum of about 18 thousand zł.: a thousand zł. in cash [?] and the rest bills of exchange.

Big election meeting at the Zionist club.
Tomorrow, Saturday, at 5 p.m. sharp, a big election meeting will be held at the Zionist club in support of the list of the Zionist Organisation in Poland, number 1. Speeches will be given by the well-known Zionist activists Eng. J. Landsztok [?] and the general secretary of the Zionist Org. in Poland, N. Asz [?].
Admission for members of the organisation only.
No. 1 — Jews, Zionists! — No. 1

On Sunday the 11th of this month the elections to the 20th Zionist Congress will take place — a Congress that will be not only a jubilee Congress but also a Congress of destiny for Eretz Israel, for the Jewish people and for the Zionist movement.
It is superfluous to explain to you, conscious Jews and Zionists, the significance of the Congress, its problems and its decisive [?] influence on the whole of Jewish and Zionist public life. Today we come to you with one demand only:
Do not forget your civic duty — go with the shekel in your hand to the ballot box!
We know how dear to you is the Zionist Organisation in Poland, its 20 years of difficult and responsible activity in the field of realising Zionism and in the field of Jewish national politics in Poland. We know that the strength, prestige and authority of the Zionist Organisation in Poland are close to your heart, and we therefore believe that on election day you will vote yourselves and also move others — your relatives and acquaintances — to vote for our list.
Our list bears the number 1 (one).

Katowice railway directorate denies [report of] separate carriages for Jews.

In connection with the uproar over the separate carriages for Jews [allegedly] introduced on the Katowice—Oświęcim line, the „Polonia“ reports: We learn from the railway directorate in Katowice that this report is untrue. The railway directorate issued no such[?] order. On the railways there exist, among other things, regulations that provide for special carriages in the inter-urban[?] trains for women milk-sellers. So[?] in this case the directorate introduced on the Katowice—Oświęcim line 2 additional carriages[?] for women milk-sellers. That is where the version about introducing separate carriages for Jews comes from.
Thus[?] the Katowice railway directorate denies it.
—o—
Reduced-fare journeys for children on the railways.
The railway directorate introduced, for a period of 11 days, reduced-fare journeys for children on the railways; from the 13th to the 23rd of this month every adult — with a normal or a reduced ticket — could take along 5 children aged up to 14, paying for them only one eighth of the fare. The reduction was given in such a way that in one direction one enjoyed 25 per cent, and for the return journey one received an entirely free ticket.
The total of the collection drive for Działoszyce, in Sosnowiec.

On Wednesday evening, under the chairmanship of the kehilla councillor (parnas) Mr B. Jasny, a meeting took place of the relief committee for those afflicted by the flood in Działoszyce.
Present were Messrs Bezalel Erlich (treasurer), Bernsztajn (secretary), Israel Poluszniecki, L. Sklarski[?], Icchak Baum, Israel Lewensztajn, Linder, Szrajber, M. A. Tapiel[?], S. Zaks, A. Fridman, T. Jasne[?], A. Szerman, Ajzenberg, Kasplewicki[?], Ch. Wiszank[?], M. Cyronowski[?] and Poluszer[?] Fruchs[?].

From the report that was given[?] it emerges that the committee was active, thanks to which 2 256 zł., 400 kilos of linen and clothing, and also 13 pairs of tefillin were collected.
Then it was decided to delegate Mr Bernard Jasny to take the sum to Działoszyce.
At the meeting the victims of the flood were also honoured.

Katowice: A Burglary / Chinese Arrested / A Burglary at the Jewish Kehilla / Transit Traffic Abolished / Father Kills His 6-Year-Old Child

A burglary.
The flat of Ch"m [Chaim] Gitsfeld in Katowice was broken into; thieves got in and took 150 zł in cash and various clothes worth about 6000 zł.
—o—
Chinese arrested.
In Rybnik two Chinese men were arrested who, in the role of peddlers, had carried out a series of thefts.
—o—
A burglary at the Jewish kehilla.
The office of the local Jewish kehilla on Młyńska ["Mlinarska"] Street was broken into. The thieves took small items. The police carried out an investigation and detained one of the burglars, a Katowice resident.
—o—
Transit traffic abolished.
From the 15th of this month rail transit through the German "corridor" is abolished, for example from Chebzie[?] to Tarnowskie Góry[?], from Kochłowice to Lubliniec, and so on. Travel in that direction will be exclusively by the Polish railway line.
—o—
Father kills his 6-year-old child.
In the village of Palik[?], near Katowice, the peasant Józef Gudojarek[?], a re-emigrant[?] from Brazil, killed his 6-year-old son with an axe because the boy, while playing, had taken out of the cupboard[?] the father's entire savings and thrown them into the burning stove.
What's New in Upper Silesia? — Separate Carriages for Jews. What Does the Railway Ministry Say?

The "Goniec Warszawski" reports that the railway directorate in Katowice [introduced] in recent days "separate carriages for Jewish passengers".
On this the "Dobry Wieczór" writes:
As we are informed by the Ministry of Communications, no special carriages at all for Jews have been introduced on the Katowice line; on the other hand, direct carriages Katowice—Oświęcim have been introduced for passengers. Passengers who wish to board at the stations lying along that line are not admitted to these carriages.
It must be added that, independently of this, the security authority, in connection with the brawls whose victims were Jewish passengers, in sporadic cases ordered these passengers to travel in special carriages; this, however, was not based on any regulations of the railway authority.
A Fire Caused by Smoking a Cigarette in Bed

On Wojciechowskiego Street in Katowice a police patrol noticed in the middle of the night smoke pouring out of Kucharski's flat. When the flat was forced open, they saw that the household things were burning and Kucharski was sound asleep.
As it turned out, the fire had been caused by a cigarette (papiros) that Kucharski had smoked before going to sleep.
Kucharski was slightly burned.
Life in Chorzów — From the Relief Committee for Działoszyce

There exists here a relief committee for the Jews of Działoszyce who have suffered. The committee consists of: Mr. Blumenfeld, Mrs. P. Goldfeld, Mrs. Fruchthändler, Mrs. Stakving[?], Mrs. Kostczyk, Ch"H Czudek[?], L. Gringras[?] and R. Kaufer[?].
The committee collected several hundred zł and also a lot of clothing. More than all the others, Mrs. Plojmet[?] Goldfeld distinguished herself in this cause.
The committee, however, has stopped its activity, because a large part of the committee has scattered to take the fresh air and has not finished its work. The committee has forgotten the plight of its brothers and sisters from Działoszyce, who have been forced to come down to begging for bread. It is necessary that all the committees for Działoszyce form a central committee and proceed to distribute fairly the money collected, together with the clothing, to the needy Jews of Działoszyce.
The Jewish Community of Chorzów — Without a Talmud Torah

The local Jewish population deserves the sharpest reproach for the fact that in such a town there is no Talmud Torah for the poor Jewish children, so that they should not grow up ignorant and empty. The worshippers of the Beit Midrash, of Mizrachi, of R' Yakile's[?] shtibl and of the Shomrei Shabbat shtibl must elect delegations and set a conference, in order to establish a Talmud Torah in Chorzów.
Poor Jewish Children Sent to Summer Quarters

Last Friday 50 poor Jewish schoolchildren were sent from Chorzów to Rabka for 4 weeks. Supervision of the children was taken on by the community representative Mr. Waller[?].
Before departure the children were clothed by the ladies interested in poor Jewish children: Mrs. Eng. Unger, Mrs. Eng. Kronfeld, Mrs. Rabiner, Dr. Kalberg and Mrs. Bittner, to whom the parents of the above-mentioned children express their heartfelt thanks.
For "Trading on Shabbat"... / A Jewish Baker Is Needed / Attention, Chorzów Readers!

On Shabbat Jewish butchers who come to the market to collect money[?] from the Christian butchers for meat they had supplied were beaten up. The police detained one [of the attackers] as he was wounding a Jew with a bottle.
—o—
A Jewish baker is needed.
The local Jewish population needs a good Jewish baker, who would make an ample living, because in such a Jewish community there lives 1 Jewish baker, who is not able to supply all the Jewish customers with his baked goods.
Menachem.
—o—
Attention, Chorzów readers!
All readers of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" in Chorzów are requested to pay honestly for the paper to our collaborator Bogomolny.
Communiqué from the Będzin Small Traders' Association

In connection with the forthcoming restrictions on the trade in tobacco products, we call upon all merchants who deal in tobacco products to register at the secretariat of our association during normal office hours.
— The million campaign initiated by "CEKABE" has the task of giving productive and constructive help to the existing livelihood outlets, as well as creating new sources of livelihood for declassed and impoverished Jews.
We, as representatives of the merchant class, have put forward a proposal to allocate from it a certain sum for merchants and small traders for investment purposes, i.e. for those merchants who need to rebuild their shop fittings and have no means for it.
In order to establish to what extent the help is needed, we appeal to all merchants who wish to benefit from this help to register as quickly as possible at our secretariat, which gives information in the relevant matters.
Big Fire in Poręba.

On Tuesday towards evening a fire broke out, from an unknown cause, in the „Poręba“ factory. The fire brigades of the Zawiercie[?] and Olkusz districts took part in the rescue operation. The damage amounts to several tens of thousands of złoty.
Rabbi Chamides' Conference on Registry Matters.

In connection with the leave of Rabbi Chamides[?], which begins on the 20th of this month, Rabbi Chamides conferred last week with the competent authorities in Będzin on how to arrange all matters connected with keeping the civil registers (metrical books) during the period of his leave.
At this conference the whole procedure was laid down for how Rabbi Chamides can enjoy his leave without a substitute and without any disruption to the normal functioning of the registry matters.
On this occasion attention was drawn once again to the fact that, regarding the akt ślubny [marriage certificate], all those who intend to settle such a matter within the period mentioned should apply to the rabbinate office next Monday, when the office will be open from 3 in the afternoon.
It would then be made possible [?] ... [for those who] would want to settle their acts later as well [?] — for after the 20th no akt ślubny whatsoever will be signed.

The Ne'emanim Are „Victims“ of the Nine Days..
The licensed butchers in Będzin have, because of the Nine Days, done away with the ne'emanim [kashrut supervisors]. The ne'emanim — they say — hinder the sale of meat, because there are many Hasidic customers who do not want to buy meat during the Nine Days in the presence of the ne'emanim.
Dąbrowa — Conflict between the Chevra Kadisha and the New Kehilla President.

Things have become a little lively in the local Jewish world. This happened because of the „excesses“[?] of the local Chevra Kadisha [burial society].
The story is as follows: a few weeks ago a young Jewish man died here, and the Chevra Kadisha took 60 zł. from the „hekhsl“[?].
The new kehilla president, Mr. Freund, learned of this levy and reacted [—?] against the action of the Chevra Kadisha. The latter felt insulted by this and summoned the kehilla president to a court of honour. In his reply to the summons Mr. Freund declared that the court of honour would take place a few days later, when he takes over the management of the kehilla.
As we have already written, the new kehilla representatives will take over the kehilla offices on the 25th of this month.
Paid for the Smashed Pane.
On Sunday at about 11 o'clock a drunk came into the fruit shop of M. Hejsblat on 3 Maja Street and, on his way out, smashed a pane in the shop door. Later it turned out that after sobering up he regretted his deed, for the next day he came to Hejsblat, apologised to him and had a pane put in at his own expense.
